キャプション1: 事典にめっちゃ怖いやつがいたんだけど！！！！
A1 cha 138: お、落ち着いてください/VAR/様。事典に怖いやつ……？
A2 cha 148: もしかしたら、この世界のある要素がうっかり無関係の場所に入り込んでしまったのかもしれませんね。
A3 cha 146: 不手際があり大変失礼いたしました。もうそのようなことはないよう、完全にロック致しますので。
キャプション2: うん、もう出てこないようにして！
キャプション3: でも面白いからそのままでいいよ
B1 cha 131: 承知致しました。もう事典で突然おかしなものが割り込んでくることはありませんのでご安心ください。
B2 cha 152: ただ、もし/VAR/様の気が変わることがあればロックを緩めますので、再度お声掛け下さい。
C1 cha 137: まあ、/VAR/様って豪胆なのですね。
C2 cha 140: かしこまりました。では得体のしれぬものの割り込みを許すようにしておきます。
C3 cha 148: もし出ないようにしたい場合は、再度お声掛け下さい。

キャプション1: Huh? Did the atmosphere here change?
A1 cha 138: Yes. I have made a fresh start, hoping /VAR/-sama would face me with fresh feelings as well.
キャプション2: It's really nice!
キャプション3: I liked it better before...
B1 cha 131: Oh my! I am so glad!
B2 cha 152: This is about all the hospitality I can offer. If it pleases you even a little, I am very happy.
C1 cha 137: Ugh...
C2 cha 140: I am terribly sorry for doing something unnecessary...
C3 cha 148: But once I change it, I cannot change it again for a while...
C4 cha 172: I am sorry, but if you could please bear with it as it is...

キャプション1: So what does 'Mika Tachiki' actually mean?
A1 cha 138: Ah, the 'Nii' of Niimura contains the characters 'tachi' and 'ki,' and the 'Haru' of Haruka hides the characters 'mi' and 'ka.'
キャプション2: That makes total sense!
キャプション3: Isn't that a bit of a stretch...?
B1 cha 131: Hee hee, it was an alias I came up with on the spot, so I am glad it convinces you.
B2 cha 152: 'Mika,' as in the third of the month, and 'youka,' the eighth, may suggest some odd link, but the dates mean nothing at all.
C1 cha 137: Haha... It was a stretch after all, was it not...
C2 cha 140: In hindsight I thought it a careless alias, easy to see through, but being such a stretch, perhaps it kept /VAR/-sama from noticing.
C3 cha 148: I seem to be rather lacking in that sort of wit...

キャプション1: You talk nothing like you do in the scenarios.
A1 cha 138: Hahaha, you would think so, would you not?
A2 cha 148: So that /VAR/-sama would not see through me, I was speaking the exact opposite of how I normally speak.
キャプション2: I like the way you talk now, too.
キャプション3: I want you to talk normally.
B1 cha 131: Thank you. I know it is a completely different image from my usual self...
B2 cha 152: I have discovered a somewhat ladylike side of myself, and I am a little happy about it.
B3 cha 144: Well, honestly, it was embarrassing at first, but in front of /VAR/-sama, this is now when I am most at ease.
C1 cha 137: Hmm... It does not suit me after all, does it...
C2 cha 140: Even so, changing how I act toward /VAR/-sama at this point would be rather difficult...
C3 cha 148: It may be selfish, but I would like to keep carrying myself as I have until now.

キャプション1: Can't you do something about that blood?
A1 cha 138: Well... I have tried all sorts of things myself, but...
A2 cha 148: No matter how much I wipe it, the blood will not go away, and I cannot take off these clothes, as if I were bound in them.
A3 cha 146: You see, this is a world without the concept of time.
A4 cha 132: In other words, I am stuck as I looked when I came here, and I cannot change it.
A5 cha 164: Changes in memory and in my exchanges with /VAR/-sama seem to remain, but anything that concerns only me is as you see...
キャプション2: That's so sad...
キャプション3: I'm sure it'll work out.
B1 cha 131: Sad, you say...
B2 cha 152: But whatever the reason, it does not change what I did.
B3 cha 144: I did stab Natsumi to death, and I ran away into this world.
B4 cha 150: Even if I flee into this world, the proof of my sin does not disappear.
B5 cha 158: Yes, this blood is the proof of my sin. A brand I can never outrun, however far I go.
B6 cha 126: I think I will simply accept it now.
B7 cha 142: Because what I did cannot be undone.
C1 cha 137: /VAR/-sama...
C2 cha 140: Thank you. Hearing you say that encourages me more than anything.
C3 cha 148: I am ready to chase the truth with you and face what I have done.
C4 cha 172: I believe that somewhere beyond that, there is a way to wipe away this blood.
D2 cha 145: I understand that, but...
D3 cha 140: Honestly, that rather hurts...
D4 cha 168: Smiling and chatting cheerfully looking like this must be very creepy indeed...
D5 cha 140: But that cannot be helped.
D6 cha 140: I committed a sin that grave and fled here, after all.

キャプション1: When you bow, a lot shows...
A4 cha 132: Um... I do not quite follow what you mean...
キャプション2: Oh, then never mind
キャプション3: Your cleavage...
B2 cha 152: Hmm... What's that about...
B3 cha 144: Well, if /VAR/-sama says never mind, I will not worry about it, but...
B4 cha 150: Hmm... What could it be...
C1 cha 137: Cleavage...?
C2 cha 140: Ah! Wait! /VAR/-sama! Just where were you looking!
C3 cha 148: Ah, no... If you hadn't pointed it out, I probably wouldn't have noticed. I'm sorry.
C4 cha 172: As you know, I'm rather careless, or rather, I have a side that lacks delicacy...
C5 cha 133: Hmm... I'll probably forget again right away...
C6 cha 135: If I forget again and something happens to show... um... I'd appreciate it if you pretended not to see...
C7 cha 142: Mom kept telling me to fix this side of me, too... How did I turn out like this...

キャプション1: By the way, what's that bar in the upper right?
A2 cha 148: I am sorry, but I cannot see anything from where I am...
A3 cha 146: This world has come to reflect /VAR/-sama's will as well. If so, should we take it that something /VAR/-sama wants to see has taken form?
A4 cha 132: Does anything come to mind?
キャプション2: Your affection level?
B1 cha 131: I see...!
B2 cha 152: Indeed, my feelings do change somewhat as I talk with /VAR/-sama.
B3 cha 144: And that has taken form so that /VAR/-sama can see it...
B4 cha 150: Hmm... That is a little embarrassing...
B5 cha 158: I mean, /VAR/-sama gets to see how I feel, right?
B6 cha 126: Somehow... that feels more embarrassing than being seen naked...
B7 cha 142: Ah! That doesn't mean I'm actually going to let you see me naked! I can't take these clothes off anyway!
B9 cha 118: Nobody even said anything, so why am I getting so worked up...

キャプション1: What do I get for raising your affection?
A1 cha 138: Hmm... What do you get...?
A2 cha 148: Even now, as /VAR/-sama's partner, I intend to go with you all the way and see this world through to its end.
A3 cha 146: So however much my feelings change, I do not think I will ever hold /VAR/-sama back, but...
A4 cha 132: But if it were to have any effect...
A5 cha 164: perhaps it would be when /VAR/-sama's thinking and mine part ways decisively.
A6 cha 146: Should anything sour things between /VAR/-sama and me, that affection, that is, our trust, may decide whether it can be repaired.
キャプション2: A falling-out?
キャプション3: So higher affection is better, then
B1 cha 131: That is, if we were to have a falling-out...
B2 cha 152: But I cannot even imagine what could make /VAR/-sama and me fall out.
B3 cha 144: You have come this far with me. Now I think it is my turn to help /VAR/-sama learn the truth.
B4 cha 150: So, um...
B5 cha 158: even if we do have a falling-out, I hope you will not abandon me.
B6 cha 126: There is bound to be some way to resolve it...
C1 cha 137: Well, yes. I think there is no harm in raising it.
C2 cha 140: This world reflects my will, and /VAR/-sama's will.
C3 cha 148: I want to believe that if our feelings become one, it will lead to the truly happy ending that /VAR/-sama and I wish for.
C4 cha 172: No, I am sure it will.

キャプション1: Why /立木/ killed Natsumi Kogori
A1 cha 138: It seems this green eye has something to do with it.
A2 cha 148: You kill even when you do not want to kill. That is the curse-killing. And what brings on that curse-killing is this green eye.
A3 cha 146: As Momoko Goto said, touch the blood of the second generation, the precognitive, and you feel irresistible murderous intent toward their kind.
A4 cha 132: Indeed, when Kotaro Niimura attacked us under the Arata settlement and Natsumi was cut with the nata, her blood splashed onto me.
A5 cha 164: To think such a small thing could lead to this...
キャプション2: At least you know the cause now
キャプション3: It's not /立木/'s fault
キャプション4: It was nothing but bad luck
B1 cha 131: Yes. I did not understand how that could have happened.
B2 cha 152: But with the cause appearing before us like that, I was able to learn why I killed her.
B3 cha 144: Perhaps that alone was a good thing.
C1 cha 137: /VAR/-sama...
C2 cha 140: Thank you for your kindness.
C3 cha 148: I do not mean to defend myself, but there was an outside cause like that behind my killing Natsumi.
C4 cha 172: As you say, it happened against my will.
C5 cha 133: But...
C6 cha 135: it does not change the fact that I killed Natsumi.
C7 cha 142: Even now, these hands still feel the moment I stabbed Natsumi―
C8 cha 106: I am terribly sorry, /VAR/-sama. You were so kind, and I answered with such gloomy words.
D1 cha 134: Bad luck, is it...
D2 cha 145: Perhaps it can be written off as bad luck, but of all people, for me to be the one who killed Natsumi...
D3 cha 140: Not that anyone else would have been better, but I cannot escape the guilt and terror of killing Natsumi with my own hands.
D4 cha 168: Natsumi...

キャプション1: Is Momoko Goto a siscon?
A1 cha 138: If you call her a siscon, I suppose she may well be.
A2 cha 148: That said, going from my mother killing her sister to killing every last person in the settlement does seem too great a leap...
A3 cha 146: But honestly, I understand how she felt. If Natsumi, my sister and my best friend, were killed...
A4 cha 132: I am in no position to say this, having killed Natsumi with my own hands, but I am sure I would not forgive the culprit either.
キャプション2: Even if the culprit were your own mother?
キャプション3: You both really care about your little sisters
B2 cha 152: When you put it that way, I do not know what to say... I could never imagine taking revenge on Mom, of course...
B3 cha 144: To Momoko Goto, though, my mother is a stranger who killed her sister and is behind the Megasawa City and flaying cases: a villain, plainly.
B4 cha 150: In that case, perhaps it is not so unreasonable that she went to such lengths.
B5 cha 158: Still, when it was my own mother who set it all in motion and led to that ending, I cannot help feeling guilty too.
B6 cha 126: After all, it all began when I, child though I was, tried to curse someone to death.
C1 cha 137: Yes. To me Natsumi was irreplaceable, and I am sure it was the same for Momoko Goto.
C2 cha 140: No, but we were best friends before we ever knew we were sisters.
C3 cha 148: I do not mean to compete, but I am confident I cherished Natsumi far, far more than Momoko Goto cherished her sister.
C4 cha 172: Because no matter what happened, I would never push Natsumi away.

キャプション1: Kana Niimura had gotten so grown-up
A1 cha 138: Yes, yes, that surprised me too. She is nothing like the Kana I know...
A2 cha 148: To think someone can change so much in just 4 years.
キャプション2: What kind of kid is Kana Niimura, to /立木/?
キャプション3: She really has grown up
B1 cha 131: As you saw before, she was a vulgar kid who, for a grade schooler, did nothing but tell me dirty jokes...
B2 cha 152: But she is a good kid. A child who helps the grown-ups; when we climbed Arata's mountain, she carried all our bags and was first to go for help.
B3 cha 144: Above all, she has a strong will. She always keeps her promises, and she will put her body on the line for what she means to protect.
B4 cha 150: If she grows up like that on top of it, where does that leave me?
C1 cha 137: Honestly, it is a little frustrating. She was far more ladylike than I am, and brave, and kind...
C2 cha 140: Sigh... How did I end up like this...
C3 cha 148: Mom did needle me about it, you know. Telling me to learn to be more ladylike.

キャプション1: How did you feel about Momoko Goto getting her revenge?
A1 cha 138: That is quite a difficult question...
A2 cha 148: In the sense that she achieved her original goal, perhaps it was good, but killing people is still wrong.
A3 cha 146: And then to meet such a miserable end...
A4 cha 132: I feel sympathy and an ache in my chest, but in a sense she brought it on herself. What she did came back to her in another form.
A5 cha 164: What did you think, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: I'm glad she got her revenge
キャプション3: I felt really sorry for her
キャプション4: Her love for her sister moved me
B1 cha 131: I see. Indeed, it was shown that deep down she was somewhat satisfied at achieving her revenge.
B2 cha 152: Whatever the ending, she achieved her goal. From that viewpoint, it is only natural to feel as /VAR/-sama does.
B3 cha 144: But...
B4 cha 150: Perhaps I am just being soft, but should she not have held back all the same?
B5 cha 158: Perhaps her fate was sealed the moment she came to Arata, but even so, to shoot every resident dead...
B6 cha 126: Some of them must have joined the attack unwillingly, for fear of ostracism by the village.
B7 cha 142: Well, then Momoko Goto was the same. To protect her own heart, she chose revenge as her defense.
B8 cha 124: It is a cliche, but I believe dark deeds only lead to dark results.
C1 cha 137: Yes. It was painful for me to watch.
C2 cha 140: She had once reconsidered her revenge, yet she was caught up in the curse-killing and died screaming inside...
C3 cha 148: In a sense, Arata may truly be a cursed place.
C4 cha 172: It was a shame on that route, but there seems to have been a choice where the sisters reconcile, so I do hope they find happiness in that dimension.
D1 cha 134: Moved, you say...
D2 cha 145: But I wonder. I would like to respect /VAR/-sama's opinion, but...
D3 cha 140: Momoko Goto pushed her sister away for selfish reasons, then lost her and took revenge for selfish reasons. Was that really sisterly love?
D4 cha 168: I suspect she was very timid. Born into privilege where she got whatever she wanted, at some point she began to doubt her place as a big sister.
D5 cha 140: Not wanting to lose anything more, she rejected her sister and schemed to leave home― but once she lost her, she turned to revenge.
D6 cha 140: And that revenge, too: she stormed into Arata less to truly avenge her sister than to protect her own heart and her reason for being.
D7 cha 134: As someone who had a little sister myself, it struck me as something a little different from sisterly love.
D8 cha 124: I apologize. It is only my personal opinion, so I hope you will understand.
E1 cha 94: That is quite harsh of you...
E2 cha 157: Indeed, Momoko Goto's revenge was carried out on a pile of selfish thoughts and choices, and in the end she was shot dead by her own warped heart.
E3 cha 157: Perhaps 'she brought it on herself' is the right phrase.
E4 cha 164: Shooting that dimension's me and Kana was surely a miscalculation beyond her control, but killing everyone, then herself, may have come from her childish streak.
E5 cha 128: I do not know whether it is right to dismiss it as selfishness, as getting what she deserved, but...
E6 cha 124: Still, had she had a little more decency as a person, I think the result would have been different.

キャプション1: So Chigaya Niimura had precognition too?
A2 cha 148: Of course! It is just as /VAR/-sama says!
A3 cha 146: But in the Shigatsu Arc, the Arata settlement where it took place had almost no cherry trees, and the Niimura cherry gave no precognition.
A4 cha 132: Had there been cherries, it would have been no surprise if Chiga-nee had killed Natsumi at that point.
A5 cha 164: In that case...
A6 cha 146: the actions of a great many people stop adding up.
A7 cha 142: Either there is still something we do not know, or else...

キャプション1: You still don't want to go back to your own world?
A2 cha 148: It is still painful. I may know the cause now, but I did what I did...
A3 cha 146: Then again, I wonder about shutting myself away here forever.
A4 cha 132: Honestly, I want to escape into another world. One where Natsumi is alive and everyone can live in peace...
キャプション2: I'm sure the time for that will come
キャプション3: Don't brood on it so much
B1 cha 131: The time for that...
B2 cha 152: I cannot quite imagine when the time for that would be...
B3 cha 144: Forgive me. I said something hopeless. It only troubles /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 137: Not brooding, huh...
C2 cha 140: True, this may be going too far, but it was beyond my control: an accident I could do nothing about.
C3 cha 148: There is no use regretting what could not be helped. In that case, more positively...
C4 cha 172: Thank you, /VAR/-sama. I feel a little lighter.
C5 cha 133: Perhaps I should start preparing myself to go back to my own world someday.

キャプション1: What's that glowing in the topic above?
A2 cha 148: I am sorry, but I cannot see that from my side either.
A3 cha 146: But this is a world that reflects the will of /VAR/-sama and myself. It must mean something.
A4 cha 132: If it glows to stand out, I imagine it must be an important topic.
A5 cha 164: Yes: one that leads to the ending /VAR/-sama and I wish for, the one we truly want to reach.
A6 cha 146: Make the proper choice there, and the way should open.

キャプション1: Who knew Chigaya Niimura was a big eater too...
A1 cha 138: Oh? Did you not see? A Reference hinting at it was already unlocked...
A2 cha 148: But it is surprising that someone with a figure like Chiga-nee's can eat that much.
A3 cha 146: A big eater and a wild drunk... Looks like she's even worse at the table than Goto...
A4 cha 132: Ah, no, I was talking to myself.

キャプション1: Did we even need the scenario 'The Maidens' Holy War ~Instinct~'?
A1 cha 138: Hmm, come to think of it, for solving the mysteries of the cases so far, it was not especially needed...
A2 cha 148: There was that scene where Goto deduced what looked like the truth of the Jusatsu Arc's second route, though...
A3 cha 146: As you say, perhaps it was a little palate cleanser of a scenario.
キャプション2: Pretty long for a palate cleanser
キャプション3: It was nice to see another side of the characters
B1 cha 131: Hahaha! I have no reply to that.
B2 cha 152: Being shown more than 50,000 characters of an eating-contest story, well...
B3 cha 144: Still, a story needs some ebb and flow rather than nonstop tension, so in that sense it may have its value.
B4 cha 150: Above all, the characters were completely serious about it.
B5 cha 158: Oh, but there was one detective who talked the mayor into it just because he wanted to see Goto...
C1 cha 137: Yes. Goto in that state was truly painful to look at.
C2 cha 140: She lost her voice, her thoughts, her will to live. Even I cannot imagine 'how painful it is when the desire to live comes to the surface.'
C3 cha 148: As you say, in that sense the scenario may have had its value.
C4 cha 172: Goto used to be gloomy and unable to trust people, but after meeting Natsumi she was reborn.
C5 cha 133: And then she lost that support...
C6 cha 135: I wonder what the Goto of my world is doing right now...

キャプション1: So Momoko Goto runs away from home on some routes too
A1 cha 138: So it seems. She meant to leave home from the start, so if nothing had brought her and Goto to reconcile...
A2 cha 148: But in a case like the scenario where Goto lost her voice, I wonder how she felt when she left home...
A3 cha 146: Perhaps a sense of helplessness had taken root too, at being unable to do anything for Goto.
キャプション2: That's exactly when she should have stayed by her side
キャプション3: I kind of get how she felt
B1 cha 131: Yes. That is exactly when a big sister mattered most, I think.
B2 cha 152: But if she could not do it, then Momoko Goto must have been that desperate herself...
B3 cha 144: If Natsumi was suffering, I'd have wanted to be the one holding her up...
B4 cha 150: Even as sisters, I wanted to be Natsumi's support, and yet...
B5 cha 158: Forgive me. Ever since /VAR/-sama learned that I killed Natsumi, this is all I seem to think about...
B6 cha 126: In any case, how sisters get along differs for everyone. If that is the decision Momoko Goto made, it cannot be helped.
C1 cha 137: Yes. But perhaps, more than helplessness at being unable to do anything for Goto...
C2 cha 140: she simply was not strong enough to stay by a sister who had lost the will to live.
C3 cha 148: Until then her sister was well, so she could push her away. But could she push away a sister who was no longer well?
C4 cha 172: Seen that way, Momoko Goto's feelings may have been more complicated than we think.
C5 cha 133: I hope that somewhere she has found happiness of her own.

キャプション1: I heard you like pizza?
A1 cha 138: Yes! It is my very favorite food!
A2 cha 148: I like rich, heavy food better than light food.
A3 cha 146: Natsumi often told me, "You'll get fat, so why not go easy on it?"
A4 cha 132: When she did, I would answer, "No way! Goto eats even more than me and look at her figure, so it's fine!"
A5 cha 164: I care more about good food than my figure. Food over looks, you might say.
キャプション2: You've got a great figure for that, though
キャプション3: You might get middle-age spread someday, you know?
B1 cha 131: W-well, even if you say so...
B2 cha 152: It is not as though I was dieting or training or anything...
B3 cha 144: L-let's drop this topic already! I'm just no good with this kind of talk...
B4 cha 150: Oh, but...
B5 cha 158: Getting a compliment from /VAR/-sama... I'm actually kind of happy...
C1 cha 137: Hahaha, that is a harsh point.
C2 cha 140: I am fine now while I am in my teens, but they do say your metabolism slows with age and you gain weight more easily.
C3 cha 148: Hm? Then what's going to happen to Goto...?
C4 cha 172: If she keeps eating at that pace, she's definitely going to end up obese someday.
C5 cha 133: Hmm, but knowing her, she'll probably keep herself in check and stay disciplined so that doesn't happen...
C6 cha 135: Well, I should start being careful now too. I may not worry about my figure, but I still do not want to get fat.
C7 cha 142: If I ever go back to my own world, that is...

キャプション1: I heard you like Super Soda Bomber?
A1 cha 138: Yes. That refreshing kick is simply irresistible.
A2 cha 148: I am not good with spicy food, but I love that fizzy kick.
A3 cha 146: Besides, Super Soda Bomber uses no sugar, and with its faint lemon scent, the aftertaste is more refreshing than you would think.
A4 cha 132: Come to think of it, I hear there is no Super Soda Bomber in /VAR/-sama's world...
キャプション2: We're fine without it
キャプション3: I kind of want to try it
B1 cha 131: Hahaha, the people around me say the same thing.
B2 cha 152: It seems to be a drink that people either love completely or cannot stand at all.
B3 cha 144: Sigh... Too bad it's not in this world...
C1 cha 137: Oh my! I am happy you are even interested!
C2 cha 140: Though most people drink it out of curiosity and then never touch it again.
C3 cha 148: Hmm... Isn't there some way to get Super Soda Bomber in here...
C4 cha 172: My clothes and shoes came into this world with me, so if I woke up, grabbed a Super Soda Bomber, and came back here again...
C5 cha 133: Or so I say. That is a rather tactless and improper thought.
C6 cha 135: If Super Soda Bomber ever appears in /VAR/-sama's world, please do try it. Love it or hate it, it will open new horizons for you.

シナリオ名: サード・ジェネレーション
キャプション1: Was the eyeless girl an illusion?
A1 cha 138: So it seems. Apparently it all happened within the danger sense Erina Goto experienced.
A2 cha 148: The eyeless girl appeared once Erina Goto learned of the Green-Eye Curse-Killing. Knowing that much, she had to return to reality at once.
A3 cha 146: One could say that layer upon layer of danger sense within her built that whole story.

シナリオ名: サード・ジェネレーション
キャプション1: Is there no way to resist the green eyes' murderous intent?
A1 cha 138: No. I know that from experience. You are driven by an overwhelming desire to kill, and your arms and legs move on their own.
A2 cha 148: Like the reflex when something startles you, and you scream and shake. Except it is murderous intent, and it lasts until the other person dies.
A3 cha 146: I am not sure that comparison makes it clear, but that is the kind of horrible sensation it was.
A4 cha 132: Unlike me, though, Goto had some room to resist, did she not? To fight it, if only for seconds: "I don't want to kill."
A5 cha 164: No, not only Goto; Kana too. In 'Memory × Revenge × Tumor' she wanted to kill Sakura-san, but she resisted and ran out of the house.
A6 cha 146: It was not like that for me. Before I could think, I found myself gripping the knife and turning the blade on Natsumi...
A7 cha 142: Seen that way, perhaps there is some way to resist, however small. It seems it did not apply to me, though...
A8 cha 134: But at the very least, resisting forever is impossible. In the end even Goto killed someone, though it was within her intuition.

シナリオ名: サード・ジェネレーション
キャプション1: Aren't the conditions for danger sense different from the Shigatsu Arc?
A1 cha 138: Different...?
A2 cha 148: Oh! You are right! That is definitely strange!
A3 cha 146: In 'Memory × Revenge × Tumor', Sakura-san used danger sense in the Arata settlement. Yet in the Shigatsu Arc, the same era, Natsumi could not...
キャプション2: Is Sakura-san special?
キャプション3: Is something off with the cherry tree?
B1 cha 131: Hmm, I wonder... The difference between Sakura-san and Natsumi... Is there something...
B2 cha 152: I cannot say about that, but at the very least, it is odd that danger sense did not work in the Arata settlement of the Shigatsu Arc.
B3 cha 144: Yes, let us keep this firmly in mind.
C1 cha 137: Hmm, in the Shigatsu Arc the tree was withering, yet in 'Memory × Revenge × Tumor', in Shiyo 804, it still bloomed as splendidly as ever.
C2 cha 140: So on the Shigatsu Arc route the tree's dying, but on the other route it isn't...

E3 cha 157: All the more reason to think that the many mysteries left until now may also lead to the giant cherries.
E4 cha 164: /VAR/-sama, we are certainly getting closer to the truth.

シナリオ名: パラサイト・プリズン
キャプション1: Let's go over the True Jusatsu Arc's 'Parasite Prison'
A1 cha 138: Certainly. It differed considerably from the scenarios so far, did it not.

A4 cha 132: Second, Droga is not a drug but contains infectious spores. That is how it expands its range.
A5 cha 164: And third, the existence of 'divine messengers.' This seems to mean dead people who move...
A6 cha 146: In earlier scenarios too, people who should have been dead appeared now and then. Those are the divine messengers.

A8 cha 134: Is there anything else you would like to check?
キャプション2: What happened to Akane Kogori and the others?
キャプション3: What happened to Erina Goto?
B1 cha 131: I said they would live on as divine messengers, did I not. The four are Akane Kogori, myself, Mom and Natsumi.
B2 cha 152: On that route, these four are, respectively, the living first and second generations and the dead first and second generations.
B3 cha 144: It seems that Arata cherry needs these four divine messengers in order to live. Though why it needs them, I could not work out...
B4 cha 150: Most likely, we can take it that they were absorbed into that giant cherry. They did say "become one," after all.
B5 cha 158: At the end Akane Kogori said "so happy," but those were the words of her as a divine messenger. For an ordinary person, it is hardly a good thing.
C1 cha 137: Goto did not qualify as a divine messenger; she had no link to Droga, so she must have been treated differently from us.
C2 cha 140: The me of that dimension said "you will become our nourishment," so I think she was killed, dissolved, and returned to the earth.
C3 cha 148: The reason for killing Goto in the first place was "dying alone in that apartment would be too sad," but...
C4 cha 172: To solve that by saying "then let's kill her right now"―that is no longer how a human thinks.
C5 cha 133: Well, true, the way things were, Goto would have ended up dying alone...
C6 cha 135: So becoming a divine messenger means sinking into a being that keeps its intelligence yet has such cruelty as well.
D1 cha 134: My guess is that when that me appeared before Akane Kogori and the others, she drew near hiding her real purpose.
D2 cha 145: She was already a divine messenger, so she was acting not on human reason but on the will of one parasitized by the Arata cherry.
D3 cha 140: But why go to the trouble of spending a night with them like that and taking Natsumi outside...
D4 cha 168: This is only speculation, but she must have needed to take Natsumi and Akane Kogori outside.
D5 cha 140: Or perhaps it was to make Akane Kogori genuinely want to become a divine messenger...
D6 cha 140: Either way, she must have been looking for divine-messenger candidates from the start. And of course, so was Mom, who was with her.

E2 cha 157: As Goto said, the government must have known something of the Arata cherry, and tried to probe it through the special unit to study it closely.
E3 cha 157: The special unit was wiped out and the operation failed, so the government had no choice but to make Motoki City a semi-permanent no-entry zone.
E4 cha 164: This is my own view, but I do not think it was a government conspiracy.
E5 cha 128: The government studied the Arata cherry and Droga to protect the nation; sending the special unit was simply national policy.
E6 cha 124: Because if Droga leaked to other countries, it would become a terrible weapon for killing, or a tool for crime.

シナリオ名: パラサイト・プリズン

E1 cha 94: People in the government...!? You mean a crime by a public institution...

E5 cha 128: Whether it would get from those two to the government is unclear, but Mom, the wife of Dad, who used Droga―
E6 cha 124: If the government was watching Mom somewhere along the way...? That line might also yield information.
E7 cha 56: We cannot rule out the government either.

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: The difference between 'Parasite Prison' and 'Kill the Goddess Kill Them All'
A1 cha 138: About these two scenarios: did you notice they had a great many things in common?
A2 cha 148: First, that I moved to the Arata settlement, and that I did 2 years of the mountain seclusion.
A3 cha 146: And above all, that I came into contact with the Verde mummy.
A4 cha 132: The big difference, though, is whether touching the mummy changed me.
A5 cha 164: In Parasite Prison, I had touched the blood of Mom, who used Droga, so I had become the living second generation.
A6 cha 146: That is why in Parasite Prison, I came into contact with the Verde mummy's 'Blessing' and ended up like that.
A7 cha 142: My guess is that the same happened in Arata on the Parasite Prison route too: the residents went mad, and only Kana survived.
A8 cha 134: But the ending seems to be the same. Either way, Motoki-cho seems fated to sink beneath the cherries.

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: What's the mountain seclusion like, I wonder?
A1 cha 138: I have never experienced it, so I cannot say, but for 2 years, it seems one can somehow endure it.
A2 cha 148: One must get food on one's own, but with a hot spring like that, one probably never freezes even in winter.
キャプション2: Would you want to try the mountain seclusion?
キャプション3: Did you know about that hot spring?
B1 cha 131: Huh!? W-well, that's...!
B2 cha 152: Well... it's odd for me to say this, but...
B4 cha 150: I absolutely do not want to.
B5 cha 158: I mean, 2 whole years alone in the mountains!? A survival life!? No pizza either!? Absolutely not!
B6 cha 126: Only the me of that dimension would drive herself that hard to get stronger. The me of now could never...!
B7 cha 142: Come on... don't say such scary things... The mountain seclusion has been abolished now anyway...
C1 cha 137: No, I had no idea at all. Not a word of it...
C2 cha 140: That hot spring seems to belong only to the women doing the mountain seclusion. The men, and women who never do it, are probably not told.
C3 cha 148: But... that's a little strange, isn't it... If there's a hot spring like that, putting it to good use would do the settlement more good...
C4 cha 172: Ahh, but then Grandma would start some hot-spring business, and lots of people would start coming to the settlement...
C5 cha 133: Haha, the settlement would kind of change its whole look. A hot-spring inn going up would be a bit much too...
C6 cha 135: But... even so, I do think there could be better ways to use it.
C7 cha 142: Could there have been some other reason it had to be kept secret...

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: Who's stronger, Chigaya Niimura or Kana Niimura?
A1 cha 138: Let me see... judging from what we have seen so far, I would say it depends on the situation.

A3 cha 146: But Kana's wild instincts, senses and reflexes beat Chiga-nee's. In a forest or among obstacles, Kana would have the edge.
A4 cha 132: As an aside, I, who did 2 years of the mountain seclusion, could beat neither of them.
A5 cha 164: As Chiga-nee said in the main story, 2 years of the mountain seclusion alone gives no experience at all of fighting people...
