キャプション3: Do those sisters have a lot of experience fighting people?
B1 cha 131: I wonder... It was never shown, so I cannot really say...
B2 cha 152: I did manage 2 years of the mountain seclusion, so I might be able to put up a fairly good fight.
B3 cha 144: But with only 2 years, I lack the experience those sisters have... It might be tough after all...
C1 cha 137: Until Chiga-nee left for Tokyo, the two often spent time in the mountains and apparently played at fighting there.
C2 cha 140: Well, each has her own style, and they are used to fighting each other; I doubt it carries over to other opponents.
C3 cha 148: At the very least, they likely have skills the me who did 2 years of the mountain seclusion could never match.

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: What did we learn in the True Jusatsu Arc?
A1 cha 138: Unlike before, we learned many things centered on the cherries.
A2 cha 148: First, these green eyes of mine. They develop from contact with second-generation blood, and bring danger sense.
A3 cha 146: Furthermore, under certain conditions, one comes to feel strong murderous intent toward others who also have danger sense.
A4 cha 132: That is why I killed Natsumi.
A5 cha 164: And the first and second generations become the Arata cherry's final hosts through spores released from third-generation corpses.
A6 cha 146: Through this, the Arata cherry grows new fruiting bodies and spreads its range.
A7 cha 142: And Droga carriers become 'divine messengers,' moving about so the Arata cherry can be reborn as a more perfect organism.
A8 cha 134: In the end, as in the disaster of Shiyo 815, giant cherries grow. That would be the summary, I think.
A9 cha 130: Either way, using Droga drives people to ruin. It is best never to rely on a drug like that.

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: How could a tragedy like this be avoided?
A1 cha 138: Let me see... To begin with, it would never happen if no one laid a hand on Droga.
A2 cha 148: Dad laid a hand on Droga when he was in middle school. If that could be avoided, I think...
A3 cha 146: But if nothing happens, there are no clues to a solution. If Dad does not touch Droga, there will be nothing to start from.
A4 cha 132: So, granting that Dad uses Droga, how can the many tragedies be avoided? We need to think from there.
A5 cha 164: On a route where the Megasawa City case happens, it is probably already too late. If the Megasawa City case is avoided, and something else is added...
A6 cha 146: Granting that Dad uses Droga, what on earth is the way to avoid the many tragedies...?
キャプション2: Mifuyu Niimura keeps quiet to Erika Niimura about Megasawa City
キャプション3: Chigaya Niimura confesses everything she knows
B1 cha 131: I see. Without that, Sakura-san would never have thought of killing herself, and the beheading would not happen either.
B2 cha 152: It removes one candidate for the 'beginning' of the curse-killings in the Shigatsu Arc.
B3 cha 144: But...
B4 cha 150: In that case, what happens to Chiga-nee's Green-Eye Curse-Killing? Left untreated forever―
B5 cha 158: No, it is strange in the first place that Chiga-nee's green eyes were never treated all that time.
B6 cha 126: I feel there is something behind that point too...
B7 cha 142: If we dig into that as well, we may learn what ending comes depending on whether Sakura-san lives or dies.
C1 cha 137: Ah, now that you mention it, that is right. Near the end of the Saigo no Koe Arc, Goto pressed Chiga-nee hard.
C2 cha 140: But when Chiga-nee said, "I wanted to kill Mom too," Goto's deduction collapsed, and the investigation went back to square one.
C3 cha 148: Chiga-nee's line probably refers to the Green-Eye Curse-Killing. But as I see it, that is not where the problem lies.
C4 cha 172: It is certain that Chiga-nee testified to killing people of the settlement every year, starting with Shirozaki-san's wife.
C5 cha 133: As you say, /VAR/-sama, we need to dig a little deeper here.
C6 cha 135: If Chiga-nee tells everything she knows, an entirely different picture will likely emerge.
D1 cha 134: Ahh... well... that is true...
D2 cha 145: So I'd grow up as Natsumi's sister instead of being given up for adoption...
D3 cha 140: No, before that, if I'd been raised in the Kogori family, Natsumi might never have been born...
D4 cha 168: Forgive me for being personal, but I would rather not... I might lose my ties with both Mom and Natsumi...
D5 cha 140: Well, if that is the way to avoid the tragedy, it cannot be helped.
D6 cha 140: Honestly, though, I would like to reach a good ending with things as they are between all of us.
E1 cha 94: That is true too. If everyone left the Arata settlement, the curse-killings would not―
E2 cha 157: No, but Motoki-cho and the Arata settlement are not all that connected, are they? Apart from possibly the cherries.
E3 cha 157: And in the True Jusatsu Arc's 'Kill the Goddess Kill Them All,' Arata was emptied in Shiyo 802, yet Motoki-cho still ended up like that...
E4 cha 164: It does not seem to be just a matter of emptying the Arata settlement. That is probably a necessary condition, not the goal.
E5 cha 128: It is quite a hard road, but we might try looking into other possibilities.

シナリオ名: メガミゴロシミナゴロシ
キャプション1: What kind of route will come up next, I wonder?
A1 cha 138: The next arc is probably the last. As long as you wish to know the truth, /VAR/-sama, the truth will surely reveal itself.
A2 cha 148: There must be a branching point somewhere―one leading to a route unlike the Shigatsu Arc or the Jusatsu Arc.
A3 cha 146: We will need to determine what that branching point is.
A4 cha 132: Whether the branching point you predicted earlier fits, /VAR/-sama, or it is another, I cannot be sure...
A5 cha 164: Either way, the truth will surely reveal itself.
A6 cha 146: Until the next arc can be viewed, looking back over the scenarios and references so far should let us make a rough prediction.

キャプション1: Do you know about the founder of the Arata settlement?
A1 cha 138: I never heard about it directly, but it falls within Japanese history in my world, so I understood most of it.
A2 cha 148: The war between the Minato and Tara clans before the Shiyo era began. The Prince who appeared there is the one who set it off.
A3 cha 146: The Emperor's third son, he rose against the Tara regime. It went badly, and in what I learned at school, he is executed soon after.
A4 cha 132: But he survived. He survived, fled east from Kyoto, found a place called Arata and put down roots there, you see.
A5 cha 164: No one in Shiyo 800 knows this story anymore, I imagine.
キャプション2: So the Niimura family are descendants of the imperial family?
キャプション3: If he hadn't put down roots, would the tragedy never have happened?
B1 cha 131: Oh, it's true! That is what it means!
B2 cha 152: I am adopted, so I am not related by blood, but...
B3 cha 144: Which means Dad, Chiga-nee and Kana have imperial blood in them.
B4 cha 150: It does not quite sink in, though, that people of such noble lineage were so close by.
C1 cha 137: Hmm... with something more than 800 years ago, I really cannot say...
C2 cha 140: Of course, that possibility cannot be ruled out. The Arata cherry and humans seem to be closely linked.
C3 cha 148: But it is a huge organism, and the founder settled there drawn by it, so I think the Arata cherry existed before it ever met humans.
C4 cha 172: Then...
C5 cha 133: As you say, /VAR/-sama, because humans put down roots, something changed in the Arata cherry too...?
C6 cha 135: No, I may be overthinking it, but the Arata cherry's will, or intelligence, seems far too similar to a human's.
C7 cha 142: Something... how to put it... I wonder if something big happened between humans and the Arata cherry...
C8 cha 106: I am sorry. My own wild ideas are only confusing you, /VAR/-sama. I will stop here.

キャプション1: So there have been huge creatures since long ago, huh
A1 cha 138: So it seems. Giant deer can still be hunted now and then, you know.
A2 cha 148: If game like that can be had, then, people being people, it is no wonder they were drawn to the land of Arata.
A3 cha 146: But because of that, other people often set their eyes on it, and the land of Arata was nearly taken.
A4 cha 132: So they took up arms, and in the end even made Droga, which should have been shunned.
A5 cha 164: It is ironic. Fighting over that soil produced a drug like that, and even we got caught up in it.
A6 cha 146: It would be wrong to hate the people of the past for this, but history has a flow like this, and it reaches into the present too.
A7 cha 142: In that sense, looking through scenarios from long ago like that is also necessary to understand the true flow of things.

キャプション1: What kind of era was Shiyo 310?
A1 cha 138: Japan at the time was in the Warring States period. With warlords vying for power, many domains were formed.
A2 cha 148: There were those who spread their power through war, and apparently many powers that were swallowed by force and fell instead.
A3 cha 146: In such an era, each domain building up its military strength and expanding its lands was likely the mark of status.
A4 cha 132: Strategists who planned how to protect their domain, like the foot soldier we saw, must have mattered greatly too.
A5 cha 164: Also, my world and your world are fairly similar in places, /VAR/-sama, so your history may hold similar events too.

キャプション1: What happened in history around Shiyo 310?
A1 cha 138: Shiyo 310 is the year of the Battle of Taruhazama, where Ouda beat Magawa: when the Ouda house began to rise.
A2 cha 148: After that, the Ouda house expanded its power and came within a step of unifying the realm.
A3 cha 146: But for the Ouda house, originally a minor daimyo, to grow this far, it must have had help from Droga.
A4 cha 132: The period of the Ouda house's growth is likely when Droga was used more than at any other time in history.
A5 cha 164: Which means that behind it all, that foot soldier was working in the shadows.

キャプション1: So who was the foot soldier in the end?
A1 cha 138: I think it differs a little from your world, /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 148: Fujiyoshiro. Considering his birth and the events shown so far, there is no contradiction.
A3 cha 146: Fujiyoshiro ended the Warring States period and took the realm. I believe that much is common knowledge...
A4 cha 132: In other words, that unification of the realm was achieved through Droga.
A5 cha 164: But by the time of Yoshiro's succession struggle, the Droga had run out, and he tried to make new Droga his own.
A6 cha 146: As the means, he schemed to keep the Arata cherries close to him, but that too seems to have failed.
キャプション2: Didn't the soldiers who used Droga turn into cherries?
キャプション3: Did Yoshiro use Droga himself, I wonder?
B1 cha 131: Judging from the story, nothing like that seems to have happened.
B2 cha 152: The Arata cherry can only propagate in suitable soil, so the cherry trees brought from the Arata settlement withered right away too.
B3 cha 144: In the same way, even if the soldiers who used Droga had been taken over completely, they probably could not have reproduced.
C1 cha 137: Hmm... I wonder... It is a hard one to call...
C2 cha 140: Most likely he did not use it on himself. I think he used people purely for the sake of his own rise.
C3 cha 148: To take the realm, he himself had to stay whole in body. If it were me, I would not want to use such an unknown drug on myself.
C4 cha 172: If it had any side effects, taking the realm would be the last thing on his mind.

キャプション1: What if Eiichiro Niimura hadn't used Droga
A1 cha 138: Then there would surely have been many big differences.
A2 cha 148: Had Dad and Sakura-san married, neither Chiga-nee nor Kana would exist, and even if I had been born, I would have no tie to the Arata settlement.
A3 cha 146: So Motoki-cho would never have been struck by so many tragedies, I suppose.
キャプション2: Would Eiichiro and Sakura Niimura really get married?
キャプション3: Would nothing really happen in Motoki-cho?
B1 cha 131: Knowing those two, they would have come together eventually, even if it took time.
B2 cha 152: Then what would've happened to Kotaro-san... There are no women his age, so he'd look for one somewhere else...?
B3 cha 144: Perhaps Dad would have settled in Arata and Kotaro-san would have left the settlement.
B4 cha 150: Then Dad and Sakura-san's children would live in Arata, and perhaps those children would have green eyes too...
B5 cha 158: Hmm... Somehow I get the feeling they'd follow the same kind of fate...
B6 cha 126: Well, it would probably turn into a different story, though.
B7 cha 142: At the very least, since Mom would have no ties to Arata, Motoki-cho and the Arata settlement would have no ties either.
C1 cha 137: Eh? Does that question even come up? After all, if Dad had not gone to Motoki-cho―
C2 cha 140: No, wait a second...?
C3 cha 148: The goshinboku in Central Park appeared long before Dad was born, did it not.
C4 cha 172: If that is an Arata cherry, does that mean the Arata settlement and Motoki-cho were already connected somehow?
C5 cha 133: Even if they were, I have no idea what that connection could be...
C6 cha 135: If so, I believe that mystery will be solved in time too. This arc exists to chase the truth, after all.

キャプション1: What do you think about the bullying of Sakura Niimura?
A1 cha 138: Let me see... I was bullied too, but the cause seems to have been different for Sakura-san and me.
A2 cha 148: In my case, it started when I stood up for a classmate who was being bullied.
A3 cha 146: In Sakura-san's case, she was too popular with the boys, and it ended up earning the girls' envy.
A4 cha 132: I think Sakura-san was desperately trying to endure it. She was someone who thought it was fine as long as she alone bore it.
A5 cha 164: Which is why she must have hated troubling Dad and Kotaro-san.
キャプション2: So Sakura Niimura was as popular as she seems?
キャプション3: What could /立木/ beat Sakura Niimura at?
B1 cha 131: Yes, I think you would understand if you met her, /VAR/-sama. Even a woman could not help admiring her.
B2 cha 152: She was beautiful, of course, but she was also kind to everyone without distinction.
B3 cha 144: From what I have heard, she was especially quick to reach out to people in trouble.
B4 cha 150: If someone got hurt, she would go with them to the nurse's office at once; if someone forgot an eraser, she would cut hers and share it.
B5 cha 158: She would pair up with whoever was left over and talk to those always on their own. Boy or girl, gloomy or outgoing, mind you!
B6 cha 126: Any boy would fall for her, would he not? She was kind to them with no ulterior motive at all.
B7 cha 142: But perhaps she was a little too kind. Both in why she was bullied and in why Dad got hurt.
B8 cha 124: Sakura-san truly had a wonderful character. But... sometimes that is the root of misfortune.
B9 cha 118: I do not mean to speak ill of Sakura-san, but moderation is best in all things.
C1 cha 137: /大文字/Huuuh?
C2 cha 140: No no no no, wait wait wait wait! Something I can beat Sakura-san at!? There's no way that exists!
C3 cha 148: If anything, maybe height and youth!? And I didn't earn those through any effort of mine!
C4 cha 172: Oh, but maybe I could win on geography grades?
C5 cha 133: And maybe I'd do pretty well in a cooking contest too...?
C6 cha 135: That's right! Sakura-san was a bad drunk, just like Chiga-nee! I probably won't end up like that!
C7 cha 142: And, and, I absolutely won't lose to her in my love for Super Soda Bomber either!
C8 cha 106: Well, what do you know! I've got plenty I can win at! Ahahahaha!
C9 cha 112: Haah... What is this inferiority complex...

キャプション1: Where did the falsificaso sent to Mifuyu Niimura go?
A1 cha 138: Yes, I have the very same question.
A2 cha 148: The Droga went to Mom to test falsificaso on people. I believe that was Kotaro-san's own call, but without falsificaso it is pointless...
キャプション2: He forgot to send it?
キャプション3: Mifuyu Niimura didn't notice it?
B1 cha 131: Indeed, that is certainly a possibility.
B2 cha 152: But what bothers me is that, as we saw in the Wabigoto Arc's 'The Courage I Wished For', detailed instructions for using Droga were written down.
B3 cha 144: Even if he forgot to send it, is it not unnatural that nothing at all was written about falsificaso?
B4 cha 150: Or perhaps the instructions for Droga and falsificaso were written on separate sheets...
B5 cha 158: Even so, that feels too much of a coincidence. Kotaro-san failing to send both...
B6 cha 126: I cannot help feeling there is something behind it.
C1 cha 137: Ah, I see! That is certainly possible!
C2 cha 140: She found the Droga in the box, but was so taken with it that she overlooked the falsificaso...
C3 cha 148: But the Kogori couple checked the box too. For all three to miss it, it must have been packed to be that hard to find, no?
C4 cha 172: Since the falsificaso mattered most, I think it should have been packed where it was easiest to see. Kotaro-san would surely know that much...
C5 cha 133: But saying so here gets us nowhere. Even 'every character was a fool' does make sense, after a fashion.
D1 cha 134: I also think that is the most likely. Otherwise, it cannot be explained.
D2 cha 145: But only Kotaro-san and Sakura-san knew a package was being sent to Mom. And only Kotaro-san meant to send falsificaso.
D3 cha 140: Sakura-san might have noticed and taken it out, but then she would surely have taken the Droga too, would she not?
D4 cha 168: If someone took it out, it was someone other than these two. Someone noticed what these two were doing.
D5 cha 140: But there is nothing to tell us who that was...
D6 cha 140: What we can say is that whoever took it wanted Mom and the other perpetrators of the Megasawa City case to use Droga.
D7 cha 134: And taking out the falsificaso means they wanted them infected with the spores.
D8 cha 124: In other words, someone who knows the nature of the Arata cherry well.
D9 cha 130: Who that could be... It is hard to guess...

キャプション1: Would you want to try Droga?
A1 cha 138: Heavens, of course not.
A2 cha 148: Is what I would like to say, but...
A3 cha 146: Honestly, I am curious. What happens when a human's full power is unleashed? One never gets the chance to experience that.
A4 cha 132: But the price is far too great, so I would not use it. Becoming a seedbed for cherries is the last thing I want.
A5 cha 164: So if it had no side effects at all, I might try it.
A6 cha 146: What about you, /VAR/-sama? If it had no side effects at all, would you want to try it?
キャプション2: I'd want to (out of curiosity)
キャプション3: I'd want to (there's something I'd actually do with Droga)
B1 cha 131: I thought so. If you could feel your full power with no price at all.
B2 cha 152: If it were me... let me see...
B3 cha 144: I would love to jump with all my might! Going all out, I bet I could clear about 5 meters!
B4 cha 150: And I would love to run as fast as I can! At that speed, I could surely run across water like a ninja!
B5 cha 158: Oh, but... If I did that at sea, by the time the drug wore off I would be far out over deep water, would I not? And if I drowned right there...
B6 cha 126: Listen to me, I always end up imagining some silly punchline.
B7 cha 142: Either way, you could do things you normally never get to experience, of your own will.
B8 cha 124: It must feel something like being on the moon.
C1 cha 137: Oh! Ohh...! That is candid of you...
C2 cha 140: What you would actually do, /VAR/-sama... Doping in sports or something?
C3 cha 148: Ah! Surely you do not mean to cause something like the Megasawa City case...!?
C4 cha 172: W-well, I will refrain from asking about that. It is not my place to pry that far.
C5 cha 133: But it is true that without side effects, it seems very practical.
D1 cha 134: Ahaha, I agree. Gaining such power does come with a certain fear.
D2 cha 145: I believe that seeing a new world means discarding the values you have held until now. Whether those values are good or bad.
D3 cha 140: I certainly do not think using Droga at the cost of those is a good thing. It might change your whole outlook on life.
D4 cha 168: Even with no physical side effects, one cannot say you would lose nothing.
E1 cha 94: Oh? Not tempted at all? Is it just me being strange?
E2 cha 157: Hmm, I think it'd be fun, though... Just once, like a little amusement-park ride...
E3 cha 157: Hm? I've seen what I just said somewhere before...?
E4 cha 164: That is it! An anti-stimulant-drug poster! Its slogan said, 'That one time can ruin the one life you have'!
E5 cha 128: As you say, /VAR/-sama, perhaps even being interested in such a thing is wrong.
E6 cha 124: Even if you only use it in your imagination, the desire grows until you act on it in the real world.
E7 cha 56: Not that I am one to lecture, of course.

キャプション1: Chigaya Niimura saw the moment of the beheading?
A1 cha 138: So it seems. Strictly speaking, Grandma and Kana did too.
A2 cha 148: Chiga-nee kept quiet about it all along because Kotaro-san could have been taken for the one who killed Sakura-san.
A3 cha 146: That is one of the things Chiga-nee kept secret: the truth of Sakura-san's beheading case.
キャプション2: Way too much about it doesn't add up
キャプション3: Why didn't Chigaya Niimura tell anyone?
B1 cha 131: Yes, I think so too.
B2 cha 152: First, the very idea that Grandma tried to push Sakura-san off is strange. She was leaning out, holding Sakura-san's hand, and then to push her off...
B3 cha 144: And suddenly cutting off Sakura-san's head is strange in itself. Even to protect Grandma, that is no easy thing to do.
B4 cha 150: But I do not think Grandma's actions were that strange. She could not save Sakura-san, so she felt responsible. Hence 'as good as if I killed her.'
B5 cha 158: On top of that, Kotaro-san cutting off the head like that made it even harder for Grandma to tell anyone the truth.
B6 cha 126: It is as if everything had been calculated. It all happened so suddenly, which makes how it flowed all the more unnatural.
B7 cha 142: We will need to be careful about this part too.
C1 cha 137: There seems to be no doubt that Kotaro-san is the very one who cut off Sakura-san's head.
C2 cha 140: So even if Sakura-san was already dead before her head was cut off, the other residents could not be allowed to learn of it.
C3 cha 148: To protect her father as well, Chiga-nee kept the beheading case hidden like that all along.
C4 cha 172: I understand how Chiga-nee felt... But if only she had found the courage to speak...

キャプション1: Did you talk with Mifuyu Niimura on the day of the beheading case?
A1 cha 138: Hmm... I remember it only vaguely...
A2 cha 148: We left the Arata settlement, left the car at Arata Station, and went home by train.
A3 cha 146: I remember Mom trembling the whole time, clutching her phone.
A4 cha 132: I asked, "Are you cold?" and Mom gave me a halting smile: "Yeah... a little. Maybe a cold?"
A5 cha 164: That is about all I remember. I never dreamed that had happened.
キャプション2: How did you learn of Sakura Niimura's death?
キャプション3: What was Sakura Niimura's funeral like?
B1 cha 131: I learned of Sakura-san's death a few days later. That she had fallen from a cliff and died.
B2 cha 152: Honestly, it was a great shock. I adored Sakura-san.
B3 cha 144: But Natsumi must have sensed something, because for a while after that she came over to my house to play every day.
B4 cha 150: My time with Natsumi healed me, and before I knew it, Sakura-san's death had become a hazy memory.
B5 cha 158: It was 10 years ago, so some of it is fuzzy, but that is about it.
C1 cha 137: No, actually, there was no funeral for Sakura-san.
C2 cha 140: I believe it was explained in some scenario, but there is a rule: "No funeral for those who were curse-killed."
C3 cha 148: So on the anniversary of Sakura-san's death, all I do is offer a silent prayer in Motoki-cho. Even that is actually forbidden.
C4 cha 172: Holding no funeral for the murdered may seem disrespectful to the dead, but the rule is the distilled wisdom our ancestors left behind.
C5 cha 133: I do not know the details, but there must be a deep reason for this too.

キャプション1: Would Chigaya Niimura be popular if it weren't for the booze?
A1 cha 138: Hee hee hee, I think so too. Usually, as you know, she is a beautiful, well-mannered and capable woman.
A2 cha 148: In fact, early in a drinking party she seems quite popular. Chiga-nee seems to try her best to make the meetings count...
A3 cha 146: But, well, the result is as you can guess. No man seems to want anything to do with Chiga-nee once she has had a drink.
キャプション2: Is being a bad drunk hereditary?
キャプション3: How does she even drink...
B1 cha 131: I remember.
B2 cha 152: Sakura-san was a really, really bad drunk!
B3 cha 144: Well, I suppose you could call it hereditary. Chiga-nee inherited both Sakura-san's good points and her bad ones.
B4 cha 150: Sakura-san knew what a bad drunk she was, though, so she only drank at New Year's and such.
B5 cha 158: As a child, Chiga-nee saw how Sakura-san got when drunk and said, "I'm never drinking, even when I grow up!"
B6 cha 126: Blood will tell. It must be hereditary after all.
C1 cha 137: Rumor has it she drinks rather recklessly. I believe you saw the episode where she chugged a pitcher of beer, /VAR/-sama...
C2 cha 140: The troublesome thing about Chiga-nee is that she tries to make others drink as much as she does. Pestering people when drunk, as they say.
C3 cha 148: Do you remember her trying to make even us high schoolers drink that shochu with the hannya mask on it?
C4 cha 172: I think the men after Chiga-nee try desperately to please her at first. But in the end they get drunk under the table and never go near her again.
C5 cha 133: Well, Chiga-nee seems to have learned her lesson, so I hope that side of her improves.

キャプション1: Would /立木/ like to fall in love?
A1 cha 138: Wh-what's this all of a sudden! Out of the blue!
A2 cha 148: Ah... Chiga-nee and Mom were talking about love, weren't they...
A3 cha 146: Well... it's not that I'm not interested at all, and if the chance came, I'd think about it...
A4 cha 132: But I'm not pretty, and I'm far from ladylike...
キャプション2: I think you're plenty cute, though?
キャプション3: That figure is a powerful weapon!
キャプション4: Well, you'll just have to work at it...
B1 cha 131: /大文字/Whaaat!?
B2 cha 152: /VAR/-sama! Are you an idiot!? What are you looking at to say that...!
B3 cha 144: Nobody but my parents has ever said that to me, so it's kind of...
B4 cha 150: My heart's pounding...
B5 cha 158: Q-quit teasing me! I mean, if you really think so, I'm happy! I'm happy, but!
B7 cha 142: Maybe being like this is why I keep missing my chances...
B8 cha 124: Phew... I need to calm down a bit...
C1 cha 137: /大文字/Nnnnnngh!!!
C2 cha 140: S-s-s-s-
C3 cha 148: Sexual harassment, that is!
C4 cha 172: /大文字//揺れ//VAR/-sama, you pervert!
C5 cha 133: Well, I mean... I do think my figure isn't that bad... But just for that―
C6 cha 135: I want no man who comes near me just for that! Any lecher gets kicked off an Arata cliff to fertilize the Arata cherry!
C7 cha 142: Honestly, /VAR/-sama... Don't look at me in a dirty way...
D1 cha 134: Haah... Work at it, huh...
D2 cha 145: Work at it... but what should I even do...
D3 cha 140: At times like this, perhaps the advice Mom gave Chiga-nee will help.
D4 cha 168: There is no need to force yourself to change; hope to meet someone who accepts you as you are.
D5 cha 140: Talking about this face to face with Mom would be embarrassing, but it really is helpful.
D6 cha 140: But if you say I need to work at it, /VAR/-sama, I must change myself at least a little.
D7 cha 134: What would I have to do to meet a man...

キャプション1: /立木/'s Operation: Get Popular!
A1 cha 138: Eh? What is that...?
A2 cha 148: Ah... I did ask what I should do to meet a man, did I not...
A3 cha 146: Then I shall ask in all seriousness.
A4 cha 132: How can I become popular?
キャプション2: Try to act more feminine
キャプション3: Make more of a move
B1 cha 131: Ah, I knew it... Mom often tells me that too...
B2 cha 152: My language, too, and that I should act with a bit more delicacy...
B3 cha 144: Given the circumstances, I am speaking like a lady now, but I think you know the real me well, /VAR/-sama.
B4 cha 150: Well, if everyone, you included, /VAR/-sama, tells me so, I already know what I should do.
B5 cha 158: Haah... It's fine for now, but actually talking like that for real is embarrassing...
B6 cha 126: If Goto heard, she'd make fun of me, I bet...
C1 cha 137: M-make more of a move!?
C2 cha 140: I see... That is perfectly sound advice.
C3 cha 148: So I should go to group dates almost every day like Chiga-nee, put on a sweet act and cozy up to men...
C4 cha 172: No, that's no good after all! It's like I'd be tricking them!
C5 cha 133: As long as I say things like that, I am still green. I must get used to that kind of game too...
C6 cha 135: If only I were as forward as Chiga-nee or Kana... Though with those sisters, it is surely pure nature, not effort...
C7 cha 142: But thinking about it, I feel that even without blood ties, I really am Mom's daughter.
C8 cha 106: Like Mom, I am sure I will meet someone good in time.
D1 cha 134: Hmm, my look, is it... Heavy makeup at my age is kind of...
D2 cha 145: Then the quickest would be my hairstyle? A bit longer, to show off some femininity!
D3 cha 140: My hair is the one thing I am confident about, you know!? Silky and glossy even without conditioner!
D4 cha 168: I am not that attached to my current hairstyle anyway. Maybe growing it long like when I was a child could work...
D5 cha 140: But it takes some nerve... I've had this hairstyle for about 10 years, so I don't know if long hair would suit me.
D6 cha 140: Well, there is no knowing until I try. When I go back to my own world―
D7 cha 134: If I ever go back to my own world...
D8 cha 124: I will grow my hair out. To break away from who I have been, too.

キャプション1: About Chigaya Niimura and Mifuyu Niimura's plan
A1 cha 138: We got to see what Chiga-nee and Mom meant to do at the thirteenth-year memorial service.
A2 cha 148: First, the one who started it was Mom. She went to Tokyo and planned with Chiga-nee how to prevent the curse-killings.
A3 cha 146: One part was switching places at the succession rite. That way Chiga-nee, a fast runner, would mark Kana and keep the Kogori couple safe.
A4 cha 132: The other was to bring Natsumi and Goto to the memorial service and look at the case from every angle.
A5 cha 164: She told Chiga-nee so that Chiga-nee could support them from the shadows, I suppose.
A6 cha 146: But depending on the route, the plan was called off or failed. The plan the two of them made does not seem to have worked out well.

キャプション1: Where the Shigatsu Arc and the Eden no Sakura Arc branch
A1 cha 138: Up until Chiga-nee and Mom meet in Tokyo, both arcs seem to share the same events.
A2 cha 148: What split them from there was Chiga-nee's decision.
A3 cha 146: Whether or not Chiga-nee confesses to Mom, "I am the culprit of the curse-killings."
A4 cha 132: In the Shigatsu Arc there was no information at all that Chiga-nee was the culprit, so in that case Mom was not told.
A5 cha 164: So on the Eden no Sakura Arc route, Chiga-nee confessed her sins to Mom.
A6 cha 146: That is probably the biggest and most important branch point. In other words, what we can say here is―
A7 cha 142: that part of the scheme of whoever lurks behind it all fell apart. They surely never expected Chiga-nee to come forward as the culprit.
A8 cha 134: After all, it would not only get Chiga-nee arrested but drag her family in too.

キャプション1: Did /立木/ kill Chigaya Niimura too?
A1 cha 138: No, the only one I laid hands on was Natsumi.
A2 cha 148: This is my guess, but when I killed Natsumi, the cherries that make danger sense possible bloomed.
A3 cha 146: Chiga-nee probably noticed and went into hiding. She had foreseen being stabbed by me, turned green-eyed.
A4 cha 132: In other words, Chiga-nee was aware I might kill someone.
A5 cha 164: If Chiga-nee had told me beforehand, that would never have―
A6 cha 146: But that is nothing but an unfair accusation.

キャプション1: I wonder if that ryotei Chigaya Niimura's group went to is any good
A1 cha 138: I have heard about this from Mom.
A2 cha 148: It is a long-established kaiseki ryotei in Ginza, a place ordinary people could hardly get into.
A3 cha 146: They bring in carefully chosen ingredients from all over and put serving them fresh first; needless to say, the flavor is guaranteed.
A4 cha 132: Apparently it once got stars from some guide or other, and people even come from overseas.
キャプション2: Has /立木/ ever been?
キャプション3: Is /立木/'s family rich?
B1 cha 131: Heavens, no! I have never even been to Tokyo!
B2 cha 152: Even so...
B3 cha 144: Mom is so unfair! Going to a place that nice all on her own!
B4 cha 150: I do understand it was for work, so it cannot be helped, but...
B5 cha 158: Even so! Don't you think she could at least take me somewhere nice in Motoki-cho!? When we eat out, it's mostly Zahha or Milanopolis pizza!?
B6 cha 126: And unless we're with Natsumi's parents, we can't even go to an inn like the one we stayed at before!
B7 cha 142: I say spiteful things like that, but...
B8 cha 124: Mom cooks for me every day, no matter how busy she is. In my book, her cooking is three-star.
B9 cha 118: I believe I am living more lavishly than anyone. So deep down, I have no complaints at all.
C1 cha 137: Hmm... I have never thought of our family as especially well-off...
C2 cha 140: Our car is big but not a luxury car, and our house has always been next door to Natsumi's...
C3 cha 148: To me, we are ordinary. I never feel rich, but I do not want for anything either.
C4 cha 172: However, on the route where the Megasawa City case happened, Mom taking any work she could get was honestly a shock.
C5 cha 133: From the look of it, she had probably gone into the nightlife trade too.
C6 cha 135: I do not mean to look down on that trade, but I think Mom was truly desperate to raise me.
C7 cha 142: So the Mom I know is truly ideal. She is certainly busy, but rather than wearing herself down, she seems to lead fulfilling days.

キャプション1: How many people know /立木/ is adopted?
A1 cha 138: It was kept from me too until very recently, so I cannot say for sure...
A2 cha 148: Probably everyone older than me knows. Chiga-nee knew from the start, after all. Kana probably does not.
A3 cha 146: At school, my classmates surely do not know. The teachers might, though...
A4 cha 132: Given that I truly never knew until now, I think Mom and the others were very careful.
A5 cha 164: No, not just Mom, but the adults around her too.
キャプション2: Did you wish they'd told you sooner?
キャプション3: /立木/ sure is blessed with good people
B1 cha 131: Hmm... All I can say is that it depends on the situation.
B2 cha 152: At the very least, I would want time to learn about my birth and take it in. We were nearly killed by Kotaro-san, after all.
B3 cha 144: If nothing like that had happened, I would not mind waiting until Natsumi turned 20, as Mom and the others promised.
B4 cha 150: Who I am―I would hate to die or be separated from Natsumi without knowing that.
B5 cha 158: So getting to go to that hot-spring inn is a good memory. Even if we had to go right home for Grandma's funeral.
C1 cha 137: Thank you. I am glad you think so, /VAR/-sama.
C2 cha 140: Of course, Dad died, and I was bullied in Megasawa. It was by no means all good things.
C3 cha 148: But Natsumi and the others saved us, and ever since, I believe I have met truly good people.
C4 cha 172: It is hardly shown in the main story, but I made lots of friends at school too.
C5 cha 133: Yes... until I came here... I was truly happy...
C6 cha 135: Natsumi...

キャプション1: About how the curse-killings were done
A1 cha 138: Chiga-nee believed she had stabbed them to death, but Mom's account shows they were actually bludgeoned.
A2 cha 148: Chiga-nee did not know this probably because she was a minor, so the adults avoided talking about how the killings were actually done.
A3 cha 146: Actually... this is very hard for me to say...
A4 cha 132: I had noticed it.
A5 cha 164: That Chiga-nee's account was off. That something was strange. Even before you came to this world, /VAR/-sama...
A6 cha 146: What about you? Had you noticed, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: There was a contradiction in the Shigatsu Arc scenarios
キャプション3: There was a hint in the references
キャプション4: I heard it in a chat
B1 cha 131: Ohh...! You noticed too, /VAR/-sama!
B2 cha 152: In fact, there was a decisive contradiction in the accounts in the Shigatsu Arc.
B3 cha 144: And it is a contradiction you can only see because of this world: the accounts differed from route to route.
B4 cha 150: Specifically, on the Shigatsu Arc's first route, 'The Shigatsu Curse', Grandma said they "died with their heads crushed by a blunt instrument."
B5 cha 158: Meanwhile, on its third route, 'The Last Chance', Chiga-nee said "the culprit was aiming for the carotid." That means a blade.
B6 cha 126: Looking back carefully, there were contradictions like this that only this world reveals.
B7 cha 142: Just what I would expect of you, /VAR/-sama. Splendid.
B8 cha 124: In fact, I just noticed another decisive difference between routes. And that is―
B9 cha 118: Shall we talk about that in the next topic?
C1 cha 137: /VAR/-sama, I am sorry to say the references contain nothing of the kind...
C2 cha 140: Well, it is hard to keep everything straight. It is no wonder you missed it. I only noticed by chance myself.
D2 cha 145: I am sorry, /VAR/-sama. I believe this is the first time we have talked about exactly how Chiga-nee did it.
D3 cha 140: We have had similar talks, so perhaps you got a little mixed up.
E1 cha 94: Hmm... In your position, /VAR/-sama, it is no wonder you missed it.
E2 cha 157: On the route I lived, I talked it over with Chiga-nee in detail. It just stuck with me, so I could notice the contradiction.

キャプション1: The other contradiction in the Shigatsu Arc
A1 cha 138: Then, besides how the curse-killings were done, I would like to talk about one more contradiction.
A2 cha 148: It is Kotaro-san's account.
A3 cha 146: In the Shigatsu Arc scenario 'A Body That 'Is Dead'', Kotaro-san said this:
A4 cha 132: Sakura was waiting on the cliff top to collapse. Meaning she waited for April sickness to strike and drop her off it.
A5 cha 164: But as you know, what sets off Sakura-san's April sickness is being in a narrow, dark place. A cliff top cannot possibly meet that condition.
A6 cha 146: What this suggests is that on the Shigatsu Arc's first route, Kotaro-san knew we were about to die.
A7 cha 142: Because if we told anyone the false condition for Sakura-san's April sickness, his lie would be exposed at once.
A8 cha 134: Grandma, Chiga-nee and Kana all knew the condition for Sakura-san's April sickness. He must have known we would die soon.
A9 cha 130: So he bought time with a made-up story and waited for the residents to storm in, I believe.

キャプション1: You noticed /桜/ pretty early on
A1 cha 138: Yes. Whether or not that happens will greatly affect how things unfold afterward.
A2 cha 148: What made it possible was surely Chiga-nee honestly telling what she had done.
A3 cha 146: That Chiga-nee believed 'I did it' was something truly no one else knew, after all.
A4 cha 132: Put the other way, unless they reached /桜/ a week before the thirteenth-year memorial began, it would have been too late.
A5 cha 164: Going to the Arata settlement in a holiday mood, as in the Shigatsu Arc, was already too late.

キャプション1: How do you even fight back against /桜/?
A1 cha 138: Hmm... That is true. Even once its existence is confirmed, what are we to do...
A2 cha 148: In the scenarios so far, it is a foe that destroys Motoki-cho with giant cherries; I cannot see an ordinary human easily defeating it...
A3 cha 146: And we do not even know what it looks like or what it will do.
A4 cha 132: I have no idea whatsoever.
A5 cha 164: Do you have any ideas, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: Everyone uses Droga and beats it to a pulp
キャプション3: Burn down the Arata mountains
キャプション4: I bet a secret weapon turns up
B1 cha 131: Um... Total suppression by force...?
B2 cha 152: And Droga is dangerous in so many ways...
B3 cha 144: Well, depending on the situation, that might work. Even with Droga, falsificaso can cancel out the side effects.
B4 cha 150: Hmm... But no matter how much Droga we use, I wonder whether physical attacks even work on it...
B5 cha 158: Well, that will become clear soon enough.
C1 cha 137: Eek...! Your ideas are on quite a grand scale, /VAR/-sama...!
C2 cha 140: If fungi have spread throughout Arata, as what we have learned so far suggests, that might well be effective...
C3 cha 148: But the Arata mountains are huge, you know? Burning them would be a disaster on par with a volcanic eruption!
C4 cha 172: It could end up even worse than the damage from the Arata cherry, you know?
C5 cha 133: I am sorry, /VAR/-sama, but I would rather you not do that. Then there really would be no humans left in Arata.
D1 cha 134: A secret weapon?
D2 cha 145: Ohh! That is cool! Landing one clean critical hit on a foe of that scale!
D3 cha 140: I like it! I really want to see that!
D4 cha 168: In that case, in that case! For the final blow, I want everyone to shout a catchphrase together!
D5 cha 140: /大文字//揺れ/I'll turn you into a mushroom cloud!
D6 cha 140: Like that!
D7 cha 134: Oh dear, this has turned into some sort of movie script meeting.
D8 cha 124: But seriously, a secret weapon does feel realistic. All the more so against a foe that big.
D9 cha 130: What could it be? Hee hee hee, I am looking forward to it already.
E1 cha 94: Aw... /VAR/-sama, you can't lose heart like that... It'll work out somehow...
E2 cha 157: B-because, look, this route surely leads to the truth, so everyone'll survive and get a happy ending!
E3 cha 157: If you lose heart like that, /VAR/-sama, I will start to worry too...
E4 cha 164: So let's cheer up and keep going, okay?
E5 cha 128: It will be fine, I promise! You have me by your side, /VAR/-sama!

キャプション1: Have you ever been to Tokyo?
A1 cha 138: No, I may have mentioned it before, but I have never been.
A2 cha 148: There has simply been no chance to go; there is no special reason...
A3 cha 146: Mom seems to go now and then. It seems she recently opened a branch in Tokyo.
キャプション2: Where did you go on your school trip?
キャプション3: Anywhere you'd like to go in Tokyo?
B1 cha 131: We went to Hokkaido last fall. At my high school, the school trip is in the fall of second year.
B2 cha 152: Every year, the students vote a year ahead on whether to go to Tokyo or Hokkaido. Actually, I voted for Tokyo.
B3 cha 144: But Hokkaido was wonderful too, of course. The seafood and the ramen especially were irresistible!
B4 cha 150: Good food is a must on any trip, after all!
B5 cha 158: Haah... I'd love to go to that ryotei too... I wonder if Mom will take me someday...
C1 cha 137: Yes! I already know exactly where!
C2 cha 140: Tokyo Disneyland! I love Disney!
C3 cha 148: I love the Disney characters and worlds, but Natsumi and I especially love thrill rides. I want to conquer every one, however many days it takes!
C4 cha 172: And this may surprise you, but Goto said she is terrible with thrill rides.
C5 cha 133: The human body was never designed to ride things like roller coasters, so it is dangerous unless you are trained like an astronaut!
C6 cha 135: That is what she said, but I think she is just dressing up her fear with logic.
C7 cha 142: Not liking roller coasters―Goto is missing out on life!

キャプション1: Could I make any route I like in this world now?
A1 cha 138: It is probably impossible to create and branch off new routes at your own discretion, /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 148: What unfolds in this world that reflects your will, /VAR/-sama, is only the route to the truth. Nothing unrelated will appear, I think.
A3 cha 146: Besides, it seems my will is no longer reflected either. All that is left is to give ourselves over to this world's course.
A4 cha 132: Still... there is actually one way. A way to change this world just a little, by choice...
A5 cha 164: It is for me to go back to my own world.
A6 cha 146: If I go back to my own world, you will be able to see what comes next.
A7 cha 142: By then I will no longer be here, so you will be watching on your own, /VAR/-sama.
A8 cha 134: What follows will change depending on the resolve with which I go back.
A9 cha 130: Either way, I do not think your will can change this world's routes as you please, /VAR/-sama.
キャプション2: So there are no bad routes?
キャプション3: Kind of disappointing...
B1 cha 131: Ah, I see! Yes, that is what it comes to!
B2 cha 152: Before, I could guide you along the routes I thought necessary, but now there is only the route to the truth.
B3 cha 144: The information needed beforehand―the essential bad routes―I believe you saw all of it in the True Jusatsu Arc and the True Meicho Arc.
B4 cha 150: That is why the route toward a truly happy ending is the Eden no Sakura Arc.
C1 cha 137: I suppose so. Before, glimpsing the characters' daily lives from various routes would have been possible.
C2 cha 140: But this route to the truth appearing now also reflects your will, so I gather it is what you want most now, /VAR/-sama.
C3 cha 148: Please, keep chasing the truth with me just like this.

キャプション1: Don't you get lonely, alone in this world for so long?
A1 cha 138: Ah, no, I see it as having been with you, /VAR/-sama, the whole time from the very start...
A2 cha 148: You have closed this world many times, /VAR/-sama, and I suppose that while it is closed, this world and I both stand still in time.
A3 cha 146: So I have never once felt lonely in this world.
キャプション2: What if I stopped coming for good?
キャプション3: What do you enjoy most here?
B1 cha 131: That is...
B2 cha 152: Time here would stand still forever, and I would stay shut in here for all eternity, would I not.
B3 cha 144: Perhaps that is close to what it feels like to die.
B4 cha 150: But...
B5 cha 158: I came here to escape from my own world.
B6 cha 126: Even if it ends here in something equal to death... I do not mind.
C1 cha 137: Why, talking with you like this, /VAR/-sama, of course!
C2 cha 140: As you surely know by now, I am hardly shy, and I think I am the friendly sort.
C3 cha 148: So being able to talk with someone like this is a great joy to me.
C4 cha 172: Of course, not just anyone would do. It is a joy precisely because it is you, /VAR/-sama, who came all this way.
C5 cha 133: After all, we have spent so long together. You, /VAR/-sama, are my comfort and my refuge.

キャプション1: In your world, do you stand? Or float?
A1 cha 138: Huh? I am standing, of course. Well, normally―
A2 cha 148: Oh, right... the rules here aren't necessarily the same as back in the original world...
A3 cha 146: Gravity is normal, and so is the temperature. If there were no gravity here, my hair would stick out like a sea urchin.
キャプション2: Have you been standing the whole time?
キャプション3: Has anything changed about your body?
B1 cha 131: No, that is not the case. In this Lounge, I sit.
B2 cha 152: Though even standing the whole time, I do not get especially tired. This is a world with no hunger and no sleepiness.
B3 cha 144: It is just that staying in one pose the whole time feels cramped, so I change my posture now and then.
C1 cha 137: Nothing that could be called a change. I expect I will spend my time here without growing any older.
C2 cha 140: In that sense, you could say eternal life is promised in this world.
C3 cha 148: But all this world holds is the route that leads to the truth. Other than learning it, I have no purpose for living here.
C4 cha 172: Eternal life is a truly cramped thing as well. Even in the original world, perhaps clinging to life fades once there is no purpose to live for.
C5 cha 133: It is because life has its ups and downs that it has meaning, I believe.

キャプション1: Do you ever want to be the you of the Eden no Sakura Arc route?
A2 cha 148: I never thought of it that way before, but if this is truly the route that reaches a happy ending, then honestly, I do long for it.
A3 cha 146: But it is pointless to want to be the me of that dimension now. All I can do is accept my fate here, like this...
キャプション2: But this way I got to meet /立木/
キャプション3: Sorry for asking something weird
B1 cha 131: Yes, exactly. I came here, and you came here, /VAR/-sama―
B2 cha 152: So being in this world is not all bad. Meeting you, /VAR/-sama, was truly a stroke of luck.
B3 cha 144: I do long for that dimension, but I want to treasure what I have gained precisely because of this situation.
B4 cha 150: Meeting you, /VAR/-sama, is a precious treasure to me.
C1 cha 137: No, please do not worry. It is only natural to have such a question.
C2 cha 140: I am not a child forever, after all. For now I have to stay here, and I have made my peace with that.

キャプション1: Is it goodbye once we reach the truth...?
A2 cha 148: Most likely, yes. Once you know the truth, /VAR/-sama, there will be no reason for you to be in this world either...
A3 cha 146: I had never once thought about parting with you, /VAR/-sama.
キャプション2: I'd be lonely if that happened
キャプション3: It can't be helped
キャプション4: Well, /立木/ did chase me away before...
B1 cha 131: Yes, so would I. Just when I finally got to know you, /VAR/-sama...
B2 cha 152: Um... /VAR/-sama...
B3 cha 144: Even after you reach the truth, please come here, even if only once in a great while.
B4 cha 150: I know it is selfish of me...
B5 cha 158: Once I know the truth, all I will have left is you, /VAR/-sama...
C1 cha 137: Yes, this cannot be helped. You have your own life, /VAR/-sama.
C2 cha 140: I cannot keep you in this world forever, /VAR/-sama.
C3 cha 148: If anything, I think that is how it should be. If you are satisfied, /VAR/-sama, nothing could make me happier.
D1 cha 134: Hm? Did something like that happen?
D2 cha 145: Ah... now that you mention it, right before I showed you my face, I forced you out several times...
D3 cha 140: N-no, that's not it!? I didn't come to hate you, /VAR/-sama! Back then I just wasn't thinking about what came after at all...!
D4 cha 168: /VAR/-sama... I am truly sorry about that time. I will never do anything like that again...

キャプション1: Why did you chase me away before showing your face?
A1 cha 138: That was right before you learned that I had stabbed Natsumi to death... I am truly sorry about that time.
A2 cha 148: In truth, I was on the verge of tears then. I could feel the moment of stabbing Natsumi to death drawing near...
A3 cha 146: However well the Noh mask hid my face, it could not hide my voice. I did not want you to hear it.
A4 cha 132: So I tried to pull myself together to welcome the next guest...

C3 cha 148: P-please, stop it now! Whether I'm off the charts or not is completely beside the point!
C4 cha 172: Phew...

キャプション1: I want to hear about /立木/'s school life
A1 cha 138: Ah... come to think of it, I have hardly ever talked about that. It barely comes up in the story, either...
A2 cha 148: There is not much worth telling about my school life. I think it is probably quite ordinary.
A3 cha 146: If that is all right with you, I will answer your questions.
キャプション2: Don't you fall asleep in class?
キャプション3: Do you see Natsumi Kogori and Erina Goto at school?
B1 cha 131: Hmm... In classes that interest me, I am wide awake, but...
B2 cha 152: When it comes to science, I can barely stay conscious. Afternoon classes especially―I get so sleepy, so very sleepy...
B3 cha 144: I do try to fight off the sleepiness, but sometimes my body gives a jerk and I end up shaking my desk.
B4 cha 150: Then the people around me snicker, and I am often left embarrassed.
B5 cha 158: So, as you see, it is nothing so unusual. Quite ordinary after all, I suppose.
C1 cha 137: We hardly ever see each other at school. Different years are on different floors.
C2 cha 140: That is why talking over what happened on the weekend is so much fun. When I see the two of them, that is almost all we talk about.
C3 cha 148: Ah, but...
C4 cha 172: Since Goto started at our school, she sometimes comes to my classroom.
C5 cha 133: Goto still seems to have trouble making friends. She usually goes to Natsumi's classroom, and when that does not work, to mine.
C6 cha 135: But Goto is famous, as you know, so even though we are third-years, the air in the classroom gets a little tense when she comes in.
C7 cha 142: After Goto leaves, people often ask me what I talked about with the genius girl. Well, it is always just small talk.
D1 cha 134: School caste... What is that? Something like how high your standing is at school? A caste is a pyramid-shaped class system, is it not?
D2 cha 145: Who knows? I have never particularly cared about it. There is hardly anyone at school I find hard to talk to.
D3 cha 140: I talk to people who are usually alone just the same, and I do not think anyone avoids me.
D4 cha 168: Hm? Then does that mean I am near the top of the school caste?
D5 cha 140: But then, the people at the bottom of the caste worry me...
D6 cha 140: I went through bullying in Megasawa, so I hate that whole idea to begin with. Shutting someone out is something I cannot forgive.
D7 cha 134: So I think I will try, as much as I can, to reach out to the people who seem to be near the bottom.

キャプション1: So you really hate bullying?
A1 cha 138: Of course I do! I absolutely hate it!
A2 cha 148: Partly because I have been through it myself... But it is awful, is it not? A whole group tormenting one person.
A3 cha 146: It is cowardly to begin with! People who cannot do a thing unless they are in a group, beating up on the weak―they're human garbage!
キャプション2: You've got a strong sense of justice
キャプション3: /立木/ might get bullied too, you know?
キャプション4: You're talking like your real self, you know?
B1 cha 131: Is that so? As long as one is human, I think it is only natural...
B2 cha 152: Or is it just that I am simple? I am the type who is fairly easy to fool...
B3 cha 144: But I do not mind. Being fooled is far better than taking part in bullying.
B4 cha 150: No―people who fool others are not worth associating with in the first place. Badmouthing someone behind their back is truly ugly to watch, too.
B5 cha 158: Rather than do something so unproductive, they should just say it to the person's face...
B6 cha 126: Oh, I see! Is it because they lack the courage to say it openly that they bully in groups?
B7 cha 142: Bullying really is something cowards do. It is truly foolish.
B8 cha 124: Still, I am glad you said I have a strong sense of justice. It is not often that one's true feelings are valued like that.
C1 cha 137: As far as I know, there is no bullying at my school. So I doubt the sparks will fly my way.
C2 cha 140: But... even so, one cannot be sure. Bullying is done out of sight, after all.
C3 cha 148: Being young, I may be oversimplifying, but a little courage ought to be enough to end bullying.
C4 cha 172: All it takes is for me to find that courage. If I am afraid of being bullied myself, nothing will ever be solved.
C5 cha 133: Because, look, I am at the top of that caste thing! I am sure I will be fine!
C6 cha 135: But... the problem is whether the person actually being bullied will think I am meddling...
C7 cha 142: In any case, I want to believe there is no bullying around me. And if there is, I am sure I will do something about it.
D1 cha 134: Eh!? Ah... my apologies... I got a little carried away...
D2 cha 145: Being bullied was painful, but even more than that, I could not bear watching Mom grow weaker.
D3 cha 140: I was in the lower grades of elementary school then, but it is still hard to watch your own parent wear down.
D4 cha 168: So when bullying comes up, I get a bit hot-headed. I just can't help remembering Mom...
D5 cha 140: Bullying torments not only the victim but their family as well. Bullies truly lack imagination on that score.
D6 cha 140: Even short of bullying, the same goes for gossip. Anyone in that circle who does not dislike the person being talked about must feel bitter.
D7 cha 134: So bullying spreads harm further than you would think: not just the victim but the family, and surely some who take part hate it too.
D8 cha 124: I think I may have just found a dream. In the future, I want to become a teacher.
D9 cha 130: So that as many children as possible can spend their days in peace and happiness, and grow into kind people.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～徘徊～
キャプション1: If you want to be a teacher, you have to go back to your world.
A2 cha 148: That is right. To make my dream come true, I have to return to my own world.
A3 cha 146: If I go back, then far from making my dream come true, I could be arrested for murder...
A4 cha 132: Going back really is frightening. It cannot be helped, I suppose, but...
キャプション2: Just tell the truth in your own world
キャプション3: That would make anyone not want to go back
B1 cha 131: That is true... What I did was something I truly could not have avoided.
B2 cha 152: So I could plead my innocence, and that might even open the way to my dream.
B3 cha 144: Besides, after saying such high-and-mighty things about bullying, wavering here would go against my own sense of justice.
B4 cha 150: /VAR/-sama, thank you very much. I understand what I must do in my own world.
B5 cha 158: Tell the other world what I have seen in this one, and cut off the root of it all. And face myself without running away.
B6 cha 126: But...
B7 cha 142: Please let me stay in this world just a little longer. I want to prepare myself before I summon my courage.
C1 cha 137: Thank you for understanding.
C2 cha 140: But I cannot stay in this world like this forever, either.
C4 cha 172: But I'm still scared...
C5 cha 133: I am sorry. Saying this will only trouble you, /VAR/-sama.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～徘徊～
キャプション1: What is Mifuyu Niimura like, in /立木/'s eyes?
A1 cha 138: I think Mom, as I see her, is just as you have seen her, /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 148: She never lets up on trying to look young, and she is always in high spirits to show off how youthful she is.
A3 cha 146: Mind you, that only makes her come off a little more middle-aged.
A4 cha 132: She does have an extreme side, though. Moody, you could say; her emotions show plainly.
A5 cha 164: And once she decides on something, she charges ahead. Well, I think you have seen that for yourself too.
キャプション2: She's a lot like /立木/
キャプション3: What do you like about her?
キャプション4: What would you like her to fix?
B1 cha 131: Eh? Is that so?
B2 cha 152: Well, she is moody, her emotions show plainly, and she tends to charge ahead...
B3 cha 144: Ah, I see! I am like that too!
B4 cha 150: We are not related by blood, but being told we are alike makes me a little happy.
B5 cha 158: So I think there are probably parts where we understand each other's feelings. I think Mom and I get along well.
C1 cha 137: What I like about Mom is, above all, that she always looks out for me!
C2 cha 140: Some people my age seem to find "that kind of thing" annoying, but that is what I like most about her.
C3 cha 148: After all, Mom spares no time or effort for me. There is no way I could dislike someone like that.
C4 cha 172: So I try to be careful not to cause her too much trouble. But I am still causing her all sorts of bother.
C6 cha 135: I wonder how Mom's doing right now... I haven't woken up in so long, so I hope she isn't wearing herself down...
D1 cha 134: Let me see... Something I would like Mom to fix...
D2 cha 145: Nothing in particular. I think Mom is fine just as she is.
D3 cha 140: Even that painful effort to look young is part of who she is. Far better than growing plain with age!
D4 cha 168: Ah, but... There's one thing... one thing I really want her to fix.
D5 cha 140: My mom...
D6 cha 140: She drives so incredibly recklessly! It is a miracle she has never had an accident!
D7 cha 134: However often I warn her, that one thing never changes, for some reason... Maybe driving is when people's true selves come out.
D8 cha 124: I do not want her getting badly hurt or causing others trouble over something like that. That one thing, I want her to fix.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～裏切り～
キャプション1: What is Natsumi Kogori like, in /立木/'s eyes?
A1 cha 138: Natsumi has been my best friend as long as I can remember. No more, no less. Even after we learned we were sisters, that did not change.
A2 cha 148: Looked at objectively, though, she is a bit of a narcissist, shall I say; at times I think she really does love herself.
A3 cha 146: So when people tease her about her figure and such, she gets angry in earnest. Well, as you have seen.
A4 cha 132: Also, unlike me, she is good at the sciences. She was always near the top in math and the like.
A5 cha 164: Though being good at something is apparently not the same as liking it.
A6 cha 146: Is there anything else you would like to ask?
キャプション2: Did she have a dream for the future?
キャプション3: So her figure's bad after all?
キャプション4: Where does that strength of heart come from?
B1 cha 131: What I had heard from her was, "I want to become a scenario writer."
B2 cha 152: It seems Natsumi wrote fiction of her own now and then. She was too embarrassed ever to show me, though.
B3 cha 144: Ah, come to think of it, in the True Jusatsu Arc's 'Parasite Prison,' Natsumi seemed to be working from home.
B4 cha 150: Perhaps she made her dream come true and became a scenario writer.
B5 cha 158: Natsumi is strong-willed, after all. I imagine she worked hard to make her dream come true.
C1 cha 137: Hmm... I never paid it much attention myself...
C2 cha 140: Well, she was slender, and in that sense I do not think her figure was all that bad...
C3 cha 148: But if you asked whether she was curvy, that was a borderline call.
C4 cha 172: Because of that self-love of hers, perhaps it became a complex for Natsumi.
C5 cha 133: The figure Natsumi wanted was more like... ba-boom! that sort of thing?
C6 cha 135: ...is what I imagine.
C7 cha 142: Well, figure aside, I think her face is cute. People often tell me I have a mean look in my eyes, so I envied Natsumi's soft air.
D1 cha 134: Hmm... normally she is not one to show such a tough side.
D2 cha 145: So it is just that in this world she happens to get many chances to show her bravery; normally she was a little more reserved.
D3 cha 140: I suppose she did not want her present life to fall apart. To protect it, I think she is the type to push herself a little.
D4 cha 168: Roughly speaking, I think she has a conservative nature. One who dislikes change, you might say.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～裏切り～
キャプション1: What is Erina Goto like, in /立木/'s eyes?
A1 cha 138: Goto is, well, loud. Lively, shall I say; a noisy one.
A2 cha 148: But until she met Natsumi, she was a gloomy sort. I suspect that even now there is a dark side to her true nature.
A3 cha 146: In a word, I might call it 'the darkness caught between two opposing ideals.'
A4 cha 132: Goto wants to carry herself cheerfully, while also wanting to be smart and serious.
A5 cha 164: In Goto's mind, I think, cheerful and smart are opposites: smart people seem hard to approach and hard to befriend. That comes from her elementary-school days.
A6 cha 146: So at times you can see her agonizing between them. She seeks two irreconcilable ideals, though it cannot be done.
キャプション2: I think she carries herself pretty well, though
キャプション3: Erina Goto's scary sometimes, huh
B1 cha 131: Yes, I think she usually carries herself well. Cheerful, energetic and smart: her reputation is excellent.
B2 cha 152: But for Goto, being smart is, in a sense, a complex. The smarter she is, the further her other ideal slips away.
B3 cha 144: Her relationship with her sister symbolizes it. It was not actually so, but Goto seems to have believed her sister resented her.
B4 cha 150: So she knows the risk of being smart. Yet if she threw her smarts away, she would disappoint her parents.
B5 cha 158: This balance rests on Goto's precarious sensibility. That is why she treasures people like Natsumi and me, who accept that true nature of hers.
B6 cha 126: I do wish Goto would relax her shoulders a bit about all that. Deep down, she surely wants lots of friends too.
C1 cha 137: That is true. Goto goes to extremes. Either she acts extra cheerful, or she throws all that away and loses herself in thought.
C2 cha 140: When she truly has to think hard, Goto casts off both her cheer and what others think, and immerses herself. That is her true nature.
C3 cha 148: This may be just me, but Goto's eyes look somehow dead. There are times she seems like a robot...
C4 cha 172: No, I do not mean it as an insult. It is just that sometimes I cannot tell what she is thinking, and it makes me a little uneasy.
C5 cha 133: I once talked to Natsumi about it, and she said, "That's because Goto is giving her all for everyone around her."
C6 cha 135: Indeed, Goto has never once... no, except when I said I was moving to the Arata settlement, she and I have never really fought.
C7 cha 142: It surprised me, though. When I said I would live in Arata, Goto got so heated, so raw. What she said made no sense, either.
C8 cha 106: Now I understand what Natsumi meant. Goto is simply giving her all for the people around her.
C9 cha 112: So I want her to ease up whenever she can. If Goto learned how to relax, I am sure she would feel much freer.
D1 cha 134: Yes, indeed. Even to me, as a woman, she is small and cute.
D2 cha 145: If you think so too, /VAR/-sama, after watching Goto all this way, then you think so with both her sides in mind, do you not?
D3 cha 140: Goto would surely be delighted to hear it. For anyone who can like both sides of her, she will wag her tail and stick close.
D4 cha 168: Sometimes I even think how much fun it would be if you joined the three of us, /VAR/-sama.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～伝承～
キャプション1: Could I be friends with you three if I joined in?
A1 cha 138: Yes, I think that would be fine. You would be most welcome, /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 148: But when the three of us get together, it is rather loud, you know. It hardly ever stays calm like this.
A3 cha 146: Is there anything you would like to do with the three of us, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: I want to go to Zahha together
キャプション3: I'd like to visit a peaceful Arata settlement
B2 cha 152: /VAR/-sama, do you really mean that?
B3 cha 144: Natsumi will be there, you know?
B4 cha 150: Surely you know what will happen?
B5 cha 158: Goto and I are used to it, but for a beginner like you, /VAR/-sama, it may be a bit much, might it not?
B6 cha 126: Well, it is a rite of passage of sorts. Survive that, and Natsumi will surely welcome you with all her heart, /VAR/-sama.
C1 cha 137: Oh, that sounds lovely! If not for those cases, the Arata settlement is a very peaceful, nice place!
C2 cha 140: I recommend going in summer. It does not appear in the main story, but there is a waterfall, and you can swim near it.
C3 cha 148: From the settlement you can also see the fireworks festival held at the foot of the mountain. Everyone in the settlement gathers to enjoy it.
C4 cha 172: Natsumi and Goto, of course, but if you joined in too, /VAR/-sama, it would surely be fun.
C5 cha 133: If you ever stray into this world by some chance, please do come and see me. I will treat you so well you will not want to go home.
D1 cha 134: Something you could never say? Whatever could it be...?
D3 cha 140: /VAR/-sama, surely not, but...
D4 cha 168: you are not thinking of anything indecent, are you?
D5 cha 140: No, this is you we are talking about, /VAR/-sama. Given half a chance, you would look at us that way...
D6 cha 140: /大文字//揺れ//VAR/-sama, you're so naughty!
D7 cha 134: Should anything like that happen, I will take it upon myself to prepare a paper doll with '/VAR/' written on it, so please be aware.
D8 cha 124: /小/Hee hee, it's been a while―I might like to write one again.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～伝承～
キャプション1: Is there anything /立木/ would like to do if she came to my world?
A1 cha 138: To your world, /VAR/-sama? Come to think of it, I had never even considered it...
A2 cha 148: In that case, I would very much like to meet you in person, /VAR/-sama. I think it would feel different from talking here.
A3 cha 146: What is it actually like? Is anything different between my world and yours, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: There's no area that doesn't belong to a prefecture
キャプション3: The history is pretty different
B1 cha 131: Ah, I see! The Arata district does not belong to any prefecture, after all.
B2 cha 152: I see, so there is no such place in your world, /VAR/-sama.
B3 cha 144: Which means there is no settlement like the Arata settlement, nationalized and placed directly under the state's control.
B4 cha 150: Well, I do think that is the norm. In fact, even in this world, most people do not know the Arata district is land not assigned to any prefecture.
C1 cha 137: So it is as I thought. I knew from the start that the era names were different, but...
C2 cha 140: Different era names mean different history, and that means different great figures. Some of it may have puzzled you at first, /VAR/-sama.
C3 cha 148: But it is a theory of my own that every world follows a similar history.
C4 cha 172: From undeveloped civilizations to the present day, history takes many twists and turns, and humankind grows little by little.
C5 cha 133: I think that process ends up fairly similar: a hero who unifies the realm, some chance to make contact with other countries.
C6 cha 135: In that respect, I think you may consider it not so different from your world, /VAR/-sama.
D1 cha 134: W-wait, /VAR/-sama... what are you saying all of a sudden...
D2 cha 145: But perhaps that is the biggest difference between us. You are not in my world, /VAR/-sama, and I am not in yours.
D3 cha 140: So it feels strange, people from different worlds talking like this. You and I, /VAR/-sama, met against truly slim odds.
D4 cha 168: And so...
D5 cha 140: And so... yes, you are right. I am lonely too, that you are not in this world, /VAR/-sama.
D6 cha 140: But that, too, cannot be helped; we were born in different places. That we could meet like this at all is a miracle.
D7 cha 134: So please do not say you are lonely, /VAR/-sama. Even if I can never be with you in person, I am grateful we met like this.
E1 cha 94: Ah, is that so. So there is not much difference after all...
E2 cha 157: Place names and history differ in detail, but the basic culture and thinking are the same. So we can trade views, /VAR/-sama, and chase the truth together.
E3 cha 157: I am glad it was you, /VAR/-sama, from that world, who came. Had our cultures and ways of thinking clashed, this world would have been hard for you to grasp.
E4 cha 164: I mean, if this had connected to some future like Shiyo 10000, our values would never match.

キャプション1: Why did you choose my world?
A1 cha 138: No, that was mere chance... I did not deliberately choose your world, /VAR/-sama.
A2 cha 148: At first, all I wanted was someone to share the road to a happy ending with me.
A3 cha 146: So this world answered, and the world most like the dimension I was in was chosen, I suppose.
A4 cha 132: That is why, apart from the places where the story is set, I think there are no great differences. The history may differ somewhat.
A5 cha 164: If a world with completely different place names and times had been chosen, I could not have guided you.

キャプション1: So parallel worlds really do exist?
A1 cha 138: Let me see... Given the present situation, I think it only natural that they do.
A2 cha 148: Whether there are only your world and mine, /VAR/-sama, or countless parallel worlds, I cannot say, though.
A3 cha 146: What do you think, /VAR/-sama? Do you think there are parallel worlds besides yours and mine?
キャプション2: There are countless of them
キャプション3: There's only this world and that one
B1 cha 131: I see. I think the same as you, /VAR/-sama.
B2 cha 152: Your world and mine are very alike, /VAR/-sama, so nothing feels strange―
B3 cha 144: Perhaps there is a world of swords and magic, a sterile world without even life, or a world where super-advanced civilization is the norm.
B4 cha 150: Maybe there are lots of worlds like that!
B5 cha 158: If so, I would love to visit worlds like that too!
C1 cha 137: Oh... So that is what you think, /VAR/-sama. That only two worlds exist.
C2 cha 140: In that case, the two worlds might be something like mirrors. Mirrors that both truly exist and reflect each other.
C3 cha 148: Even so, for the only difference to be where the story is set is awfully pinpoint. As if our world were this time's―
C5 cha 133: /VAR/-sama, I have just thought of something a little frightening. You may take it for my idle nonsense, though...
C6 cha 135: Let us talk about that in the next topic.

キャプション1: If there's another world, what kind would you want to go to?
A1 cha 138: If there are other worlds, I would long for a world of swords and magic.
A2 cha 148: And I would become an adventurer! I want to wield sword and magic and go on adventures all over that world!
A3 cha 146: But, you know. Worlds of swords and magic have what you might call classes, do they not?
A4 cha 132: /VAR/-sama, which class do you think would suit me best?
キャプション2: Hero
キャプション3: Warrior
B1 cha 131: Ooh, a hero! A woman hero is so cool!
B2 cha 152: Then, if there is a hero, that means there is a demon king too, does it not?
B3 cha 144: That is a class with heavy responsibility... Her strength would be top-notch, of course, but her enemies would be just as mighty...
B4 cha 150: Accepting such a harsh fate and fighting for the people she holds dear.
B5 cha 158: It really is cool! If I go to a world of swords and magic, I will be a hero!
B6 cha 126: But then I would need companions too. Natsumi as the priest, Goto as the mage...
B7 cha 142: And for the warrior...
B8 cha 124: Mom, maybe! Or Chiga-nee, or Kana?
B9 cha 118: Just imagining it is fun. I really do long for a world of swords and magic.
C1 cha 137: Oh, a warrior, is it?
C2 cha 140: Indeed, I suppose I do give off a rather militant image.
C3 cha 148: But I am simple-minded, so I am afraid sleep spells or confusion spells would get me easily. I probably would not have any magic resistance either.
C4 cha 172: But in exchange, it is a class that mows enemies down in hand-to-hand combat and becomes the main force. I would need proper gear against mental attacks.
D1 cha 134: A priest? That is unexpected.
D2 cha 145: Because healing magic and support magic are not how I see myself at all.
D3 cha 140: No, wait, priests have instant-death spells too, do they not? And spells that wipe out the undead...
D4 cha 168: Hee hee hee, even as a priest, I would show the enemy no mercy. I would wipe them out before the warrior or the mage could even whittle down their HP.
D5 cha 140: Mwahahaha! I am a cleric who annihilates the enemy! Every last heretic shall die!
D6 cha 140: Haha... that makes me sound like the enemy's strategist. Perhaps I am not cut out to be a priest after all.
E1 cha 94: A-a mage!? That seems the furthest thing from my image...
E2 cha 157: Ah, but in this world I might be something like a mage. I did wear that outfit at first...
E3 cha 157: If I became a mage... let me see... what would I want to do...
E4 cha 164: I would want to fly! With travel magic I would fly all over the world like a bird! And save on travel costs, too!
E5 cha 128: And, and, I could save on utilities too, right!? Control fire and ice, and there's no gas bill and no fridge bill!
E6 cha 124: Hee hee hee, if I could become one in the real world, it would be a mage. It seems handy in so many ways.

キャプション1: The frightening thing if only two worlds exist
A1 cha 138: If only my world and yours exist, /VAR/-sama, then each could be said to need the other.
A2 cha 148: And the differences lie only in the parts involved in this case. What that means is...
A3 cha 146: That when this case is fully solved, one of the worlds might vanish.
A4 cha 132: /VAR/-sama, have you heard of 'the five-minute hypothesis'?
A5 cha 164: It is the skeptical thought that "the world may have come into being five minutes ago."
A6 cha 146: Applied here, our world exists as a 'spectacle' for you, /VAR/-sama. In other words, our world was born for your sake.
A7 cha 142: Which means that if you deem this world unnecessary, /VAR/-sama, our world would lose its reason to exist and vanish.
A8 cha 134: Our world stands only on whether or not you need it, /VAR/-sama.
キャプション2: You mean it's a world prepared for me?
キャプション3: That's just ridiculous
キャプション4: Then the worlds must be countless after all
B1 cha 131: That is what I mean. If we assume only two worlds exist, I can see it no other way.
B2 cha 152: My grounds: only the parts where the case happened―that is, only the parts you are viewing, /VAR/-sama―differ from your world.
B3 cha 144: Or so I mused, philosophically, which is not like me. Once one starts saying such things, there is no end to it, though.
B4 cha 150: Conversely, if you thought this world unnecessary, /VAR/-sama, it could just as well be your world that vanishes.
B5 cha 158: In that case, would you be both a god of creation and a god of destruction, /VAR/-sama?
B6 cha 126: Well, all of this is just my own fancy and idle talk. Please do not mind it.
C1 cha 137: Hahaha! I thought so. The survival of a world depending on your will, /VAR/-sama...
C2 cha 140: If that were true, you would be more frightening than anything, /VAR/-sama. Far more troublesome than Shigatsu Youka.
C3 cha 148: Still, 'the five-minute hypothesis' is an interesting thing.
C4 cha 172: No world has proof that it existed more than five minutes ago. Our memories may have been planted five minutes ago, and old relics made five minutes ago too.
C5 cha 133: There is no end to that either, once one starts. Well, these were just passing thoughts of mine, so please do not mind them.
D1 cha 134: Yes, I suppose it is most reasonable to think there are countless worlds after all.
D2 cha 145: Because I sought someone to walk with me, a very similar world connected, and you came here out of curiosity, /VAR/-sama. That fits far better.
D3 cha 140: The very fact that different worlds connect is strange, so I do not think any possibility should be ruled out, but...
D4 cha 168: This is an emotional point, but it would be sad if our world vanished because of your intent, /VAR/-sama. I would like to hope that is not so.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～焦点～
キャプション1: Do you like philosophical talk?
A1 cha 138: No, not particularly. What I said earlier just happened to come to mind.
A2 cha 148: 'The five-minute hypothesis,' too, was something a teacher told us as small talk in ethics class.
A3 cha 146: Natsumi and Goto both said they are no good at that kind of talk. I do not dislike it; I just never happened to have a chance to talk about it.
A4 cha 132: Do you like philosophical talk, /VAR/-sama?
キャプション2: I love it
キャプション3: Not really interested
B1 cha 131: I knew it! I had a feeling you did!
B2 cha 152: The story of this world has a lot of philosophical talk too, especially exchanges about ethics.
B3 cha 144: Talk of human life and death, especially, inevitably comes up a lot. Everyone is acting for their own sense of justice, after all.
C1 cha 137: Oh, that is unexpected... I had the impression you would like that kind of talk, /VAR/-sama...
C2 cha 140: Well, we have seen all sorts of stories here. Things tend to drift toward philosophy, so I simply imagined it on my own.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～焦点～
キャプション1: What's ethically unforgivable?
A1 cha 138: Then, since we are on the subject, I would like to ask about your view of life and death, /VAR/-sama...
A2 cha 148: Of the following cases, which do you think strays furthest from humanity, /VAR/-sama?
